1	# AI-powered review of past commands — pipes the Nth block to a coding-agent
2	# CLI in one-shot / advisory mode (agent prints its reply; no file edits).
3	# Depends on 03_tmux_capture.zsh for `cpblock`.
4	#
5	#   aifix [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]
6	#   aiexplain [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]
7	#   aiblock                                                    # Python TUI
8	#
9	# Agent auto-detection order: claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent.
10	# Override via -a AGENT. Advisory-only by design; there is no --execute flag.
11	# For a back-and-forth interactive session, use `aiblock` → "Spawn agent".
12	#
13	# Env-var defaults (set in ~/.zshrc or a 99_local_*.zsh to override):
14	#
15	#   AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL     default: haiku           (claude --model alias)
16	#   AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL   default: github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5
17	#   AICAP_CODEX_MODEL      default: gpt-5-mini
18	#   AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL     default: (unset — let cursor-agent pick)
19	#   AICAP_SHOW_METADATA    default: 1  (tokens / cost / model on stderr)
20	#                                        only extracted from claude JSON output
21	#                                        for now; other agents print agent
22	#                                        name + model only.
23	#   AICAP_PRETTIFY         default: 1  (auto: glow → bat → raw; non-tty = raw)
24	#
25	# Defaults are set below; do not edit this file to change them — `export
26	# AICAP_*=…` in your shell rc instead.
27	
28	: "${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL:=haiku}"
29	: "${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL:=github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5}"
30	: "${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL:=gpt-5-mini}"
31	: "${AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL:=}"
32	: "${AICAP_SHOW_METADATA:=1}"
33	: "${AICAP_PRETTIFY:=1}"
34	: "${AICAP_SPINNER:=1}"
35	
36	_aiagent_autodetect() {
37	  local cand
38	  for cand in claude opencode codex cursor-agent; do
39	    if command -v "$cand" &>/dev/null; then
40	      print -r -- "$cand"
41	      return 0
42	    fi
43	  done
44	  return 1
45	}
46	
47	# Background spinner on stderr while the agent is thinking. Skipped when
48	# AICAP_SPINNER=0 or stderr isn't a tty (so pipes / file redirects stay
49	# clean). The spinner subprocess is disowned via `&!` so it survives the
50	# command substitution that invokes the agent.
51	_AICAP_SPIN_PID=
52	_aicap_spinner_start() {
53	  [[ "$AICAP_SPINNER" != "1" ]] && return 0
54	  [[ ! -t 2 ]] && return 0
55	  local label=${1:-thinking}
56	  (
57	    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT HUP
58	    local frames=('⠋' '⠙' '⠹' '⠸' '⠼' '⠴' '⠦' '⠧' '⠇' '⠏')
59	    local i=0
60	    while true; do
61	      printf '\r\e[K%s %s' "${frames[$(( (i % 10) + 1 ))]}" "$label" >&2
62	      (( i++ ))
63	      sleep 0.1
64	    done
65	  ) &!
66	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=$!
67	}
68	
69	_aicap_spinner_stop() {
70	  [[ -z "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" ]] && return 0
71	  kill "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
72	  # Drain; zsh waits on PIDs even if disowned as long as we know the PID.
73	  wait "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
74	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=
75	  [[ -t 2 ]] && printf '\r\e[K' >&2
76	}
77	
78	# Pretty-print stdin as Markdown: glow > bat > raw. Skips prettify if stdout
79	# is NOT a tty (so pipes stay clean) or AICAP_PRETTIFY=0.
80	_aicap_prettify() {
81	  if [[ "$AICAP_PRETTIFY" != "1" ]] || [[ ! -t 1 ]]; then
82	    cat
83	  elif command -v glow &>/dev/null; then
84	    glow -
85	  elif command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
86	    bat --language=md --style=plain --paging=never --color=always
87	  else
88	    cat
89	  fi
90	}
91	
92	# Invoke a coding-agent in one-shot mode.
93	#
94	# Writes reply (text) to stdout. Writes metadata line to stderr when
95	# AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1 and the agent supports structured JSON output.
96	# Currently only Claude's JSON includes usage/cost — other agents just get a
97	# "<agent> (<model>)" line on stderr.
98	_aiagent_invoke() {
99	  local agent=$1 prompt=$2
100	  local json reply model_used tokens_in tokens_out cache_read cache_create cost duration rc
101	
102	  # Ensure spinner cleans up if the caller returns or we hit a trap.
103	  trap '_aicap_spinner_stop' EXIT INT TERM
104	
105	  case "$agent" in
106	    claude)
107	      if [[ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" == "1" ]] && command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
108	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL (json)…"
109	        json=$(claude -p --model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" --output-format json "$prompt")
110	        rc=$?
111	        _aicap_spinner_stop
112	        (( rc != 0 )) && return $rc
113	        reply=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.result // empty')
114	        model_used=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.modelUsage | keys | first // "?"')
115	        tokens_in=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "?"')
116	        tokens_out=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.usage.output_tokens // "?"')
117	        cache_read=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_read_input_tokens // 0')
118	        cache_create=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens // 0')
119	        cost=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.total_cost_usd // "?"')
120	        duration=$(print -r -- "$json" | jq -r '.duration_ms // "?"')
121	        print -u2 "claude ($model_used) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out cache=(r:$cache_read,w:$cache_create) | cost=\$$cost ${duration}ms"
122	        print -r -- "$reply"
123	      else
124	        print -u2 "claude ($AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL)"
125	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL…"
126	        claude -p --model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" "$prompt"
127	        rc=$?
128	        _aicap_spinner_stop
129	        return $rc
130	      fi
131	      ;;
132	    opencode)
133	      print -u2 "opencode ($AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL)"
134	      _aicap_spinner_start "opencode $AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL…"
135	      opencode run -m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" "$prompt"
136	      rc=$?
137	      _aicap_spinner_stop
138	      return $rc
139	      ;;
140	    codex)
141	      print -u2 "codex ($AICAP_CODEX_MODEL)"
142	      _aicap_spinner_start "codex $AICAP_CODEX_MODEL…"
143	      codex exec -m "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL" "$prompt"
144	      rc=$?
145	      _aicap_spinner_stop
146	      return $rc
147	      ;;
148	    cursor-agent)
149	      if [[ -n "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" ]]; then
150	        print -u2 "cursor-agent ($AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL)"
151	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent $AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL…"
152	        cursor-agent -p --model "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" "$prompt"
153	      else
154	        print -u2 "cursor-agent"
155	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent…"
156	        cursor-agent -p "$prompt"
157	      fi
158	      rc=$?
159	      _aicap_spinner_stop
160	      return $rc
161	      ;;
162	    *) print -u2 "aifix: unknown agent '$agent' (supported: claude, opencode, codex, cursor-agent)"; return 1 ;;
163	  esac
164	}

166	# Core dispatcher: given an already-captured block, build the prompt, invoke
167	# the agent, pipe reply through the prettifier. Shared by the four sources:
168	# cpblock (aifix/aiexplain), stdin (aifix-stdin), tee'd CMD run (aifix-run),
169	# and thefuck-style rerun (aifix-rerun).
170	#
171	#   _ai_dispatch_core <name> <source-label> <default-prompt>
172	#                     <agent> <raw> <no-meta> <prompt-override> <block>
173	_ai_dispatch_core() {
174	  local name=$1 source_label=$2 default_prompt=$3
175	  local agent=$4 raw=$5 no_meta=$6 prompt_override=$7 block=$8
176	  if [[ -z "$block" ]]; then
177	    print -u2 "$name: empty block"
178	    return 1
179	  fi
180	  local prompt="${prompt_override:-$default_prompt}
181	
182	$block"
183	  print -u2 "$name ← $source_label"
184	
185	  # Per-call env overrides: --no-meta / --raw flip env-var behaviour locally
186	  # so _aiagent_invoke + _aicap_prettify see the intended values.
187	  local saved_show=$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA saved_pretty=$AICAP_PRETTIFY
188	  (( no_meta )) && AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=0
189	  (( raw ))    && AICAP_PRETTIFY=0
190	
191	  if (( raw )); then
192	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt"
193	  else
194	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt" | _aicap_prettify
195	  fi
196	  local rc=$?
197	
198	  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=$saved_show
199	  AICAP_PRETTIFY=$saved_pretty
200	  return $rc
201	}
202	
203	# Print the shared flag-help + env-var snapshot. Used by -h on each wrapper.
204	_ai_print_help() {
205	  local name=$1 usage=$2
206	  print -r -- "usage: $name $usage"
207	  print -r -- "  -a AGENT   claude | opencode | codex | cursor-agent (default: auto-detect)"
208	  print -r -- "  -p PROMPT  override default prompt"
209	  print -r -- "  --raw      disable prettify (glow/bat), print raw agent reply"
210	  print -r -- "  --no-meta  suppress the stderr metadata line"
211	  print -r -- ""
212	  print -r -- "env vars:"
213	  print -r -- "  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL}"
214	  print -r -- "  AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL = ${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL}"
215	  print -r -- "  AICAP_CODEX_MODEL    = ${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL}"
216	  print -r -- "  AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL:-<unset>}"
217	  print -r -- "  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA  = ${AICAP_SHOW_METADATA}"
218	  print -r -- "  AICAP_PRETTIFY       = ${AICAP_PRETTIFY}"
219	  print -r -- "  AICAP_SPINNER        = ${AICAP_SPINNER}"
220	}
221	
222	# Shared dispatcher for aifix / aiexplain. Captures via cpblock.
223	_ai_capture_dispatch() {
224	  emulate -L zsh
225	  local name=$1; shift
226	  local default_prompt=$1; shift
227	  local n=1 agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
228	  while (( $# )); do
229	    case "$1" in
230	      -a|--agent)   agent=$2; shift 2 ;;
231	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override=$2; shift 2 ;;
232	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
233	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
234	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
235	                    print -r -- "  N          block index back (default 1 = last)"
236	                    return 0 ;;
237	      --) shift; break ;;
238	      -*) print -u2 "$name: unknown flag: $1"; return 1 ;;
239	      *)  n=$1; shift ;;
240	    esac
241	  done
242	  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
243	    print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n)"
244	    return 1
245	  fi
246	  if [[ -z "$agent" ]]; then
247	    agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
248	      print -u2 "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH (tried: claude, opencode, codex, cursor-agent)"
249	      return 1
250	    }
251	  fi
252	  local block
253	  block=$(cpblock "$n" 2>/dev/null) || {
254	    print -u2 "$name: cpblock $n failed (run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply)"
255	    return 1
256	  }
257	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "block -$n" "$default_prompt" \
258	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
259	}
260	
261	aifix() {
262	  _ai_capture_dispatch aifix \
263	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific." \
264	    "$@"
265	}
266	
267	aiexplain() {

269	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise." \
270	    "$@"
271	}

273	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
274	# Non-tmux Tier 1: stdin / run / rerun sources
275	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
276	# These three cover the "no tmux available" case (VSCode integrated terminal,
277	# bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH) by NOT relying on cpblock / OSC 133.
278	# Each composes zero magic — user explicitly picks the source.
279	#
280	# See backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md for why we don't do automatic
281	# tee redirection (Tier 2) or PTY proxy wrapping (Tier 3).
282	
283	# aifix-stdin: read whatever the caller piped in. Universal.
284	#   tail -200 /var/log/nginx/error.log | aifix-stdin
285	#   curl -sS https://weird.api/thing | aifix-stdin -p "explain this JSON"
286	#   aifix-stdin < build.log
287	aifix-stdin() {
288	  emulate -L zsh
289	  local name=aifix-stdin agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
290	  local default_prompt="Here is output captured from my terminal. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."
291	  while (( $# )); do
292	    case "$1" in
293	      -a|--agent)   agent=$2; shift 2 ;;
294	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override=$2; shift 2 ;;
295	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
296	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
297	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
298	                    print -r -- "  Reads block from stdin. No tmux / cpblock dependency."
299	                    return 0 ;;
300	      *) print -u2 "$name: unexpected arg: $1 (did you mean -p?)"; return 1 ;;
301	    esac
302	  done
303	  if [[ -z "$agent" ]]; then
304	    agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
305	      print -u2 "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH"
306	      return 1
307	    }
308	  fi
309	  # -t 0 checks if stdin is a terminal. If it is, user likely forgot to pipe.
310	  if [[ -t 0 ]]; then
311	    print -u2 "$name: stdin is a tty — did you forget to pipe? Example:"
312	    print -u2 "  some-command 2>&1 | $name"
313	    return 1
314	  fi
315	  local block
316	  block=$(cat)
317	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "stdin" "$default_prompt" \
318	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
319	}
320	
321	# aifix-run: run CMD, tee stdout+stderr to a log, feed "$ CMD\n<output>\n(exit code: N)"
322	# to the agent. Use `--` to separate flags from the command.
323	#   aifix-run -- cargo build --release
324	#   aifix-run -p "is this safe?" -- ansible-playbook deploy.yml
325	#
326	# isatty caveat: teeing makes CMD's stdout a pipe, so TUI apps (vim, less)
327	# render in degraded mode. Don't use this for interactive tools.
328	aifix-run() {
329	  emulate -L zsh
330	  local name=aifix-run agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
331	  local default_prompt="Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."
332	  while (( $# )); do
333	    case "$1" in
334	      -a|--agent)   agent=$2; shift 2 ;;
335	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override=$2; shift 2 ;;
336	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
337	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
338	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta] -- CMD [ARG...]"
339	                    print -r -- "  Runs CMD with stdout+stderr teed to a log, feeds to agent."
340	                    print -r -- "  Use \`--\` to separate flags from the command."
341	                    return 0 ;;
342	      --) shift; break ;;
343	      -*) print -u2 "$name: unknown flag: $1"; return 1 ;;
344	      *) break ;;
345	    esac
346	  done
347	  if (( $# == 0 )); then
348	    print -u2 "$name: missing command. Usage: $name [flags] -- CMD [ARG...]"
349	    return 1
350	  fi
351	  if [[ -z "$agent" ]]; then
352	    agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
353	      print -u2 "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH"
354	      return 1
355	    }
356	  fi
357	  local log
358	  log=$(mktemp -t aifix-run.XXXXXX) || { print -u2 "$name: mktemp failed"; return 1; }
359	  # Record the command line as the block's first line so the agent knows
360	  # what was run. Use $(print -r -- "$*") to preserve args verbatim.
361	  print -r -- "\$ $*" > "$log"
362	  "$@" 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
363	  local rc=${pipestatus[1]}
364	  print -r -- "" >> "$log"
365	  print -r -- "(exit code: $rc)" >> "$log"
366	  local block
367	  block=$(<"$log")
368	  rm -f "$log"
369	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "run \`${1}…\` (exit $rc)" "$default_prompt" \
370	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
371	}
372	
373	# aifix-rerun: thefuck-style. Re-executes the last command from shell history
374	# via aifix-run. Prompts for confirmation unless -y, because re-running has
375	# side effects if the command isn't idempotent.
376	aifix-rerun() {
377	  emulate -L zsh
378	  local name=aifix-rerun yes=0 forward=()
379	  while (( $# )); do
380	    case "$1" in
381	      -y|--yes) yes=1; shift ;;
382	      -h|--help) _ai_print_help "$name" "[-y] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
383	                 print -r -- "  Re-executes the last command from zsh history via aifix-run."
384	                 print -r -- "  Prompts for confirmation unless -y (side effects beware)."
385	                 return 0 ;;
386	      *) forward+=("$1"); shift ;;
387	    esac
388	  done
389	  # fc -ln -2 -2: skip aifix-rerun itself (which is -1), grab the one before.
390	  local cmd
391	  cmd=$(fc -ln -2 -2 2>/dev/null)
392	  cmd="${cmd#	}"; cmd="${cmd# }"
393	  if [[ -z "$cmd" ]]; then
394	    print -u2 "$name: no prior command in shell history"
395	    return 1
396	  fi
397	  print -u2 "$name: will re-execute:"
398	  print -u2 "  $cmd"
399	  print -u2 "⚠ side effects if the command is not idempotent (network calls, file writes, etc.)"
400	  if (( ! yes )); then
401	    local reply
402	    read -q "reply?Proceed? [y/N] "
403	    print
404	    [[ "$reply" != "y" ]] && { print -u2 "$name: aborted"; return 130; }
405	  fi
406	  # Delegate to aifix-run via eval (preserves quoting for $cmd's shell syntax).
407	  eval "aifix-run ${forward[*]} -- $cmd"
408	}
409	
410	# aiblock — launch the Python TUI (scripts/aiblock.py) resolved via
411	# chezmoi source-path, cached per-shell. The Python side reads the same
412	# AICAP_* env vars so model defaults stay consistent.
413	#
414	# History passing: `fc -ln …` only works inside this interactive zsh —
415	# a `zsh -ic` subshell doesn't inherit the in-memory history buffer and
416	# `fc -R` only pulls whatever the HISTFILE has on disk (which misses
417	# unflushed recent commands). Dump the current shell's history into a
418	# temp file and hand the path to the TUI via $AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP.
419	_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT=""
420	aiblock() {
421	  emulate -L zsh
422	  if [[ -z "$_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT" ]]; then
423	    local base
424	    base=$(chezmoi source-path 2>/dev/null) || {
425	      print -u2 "aiblock: could not resolve chezmoi source-path"
426	      return 1
427	    }
428	    _AIBLOCK_SCRIPT="$base/scripts/aiblock.py"
429	  fi
430	  if [[ ! -f "$_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT" ]]; then
431	    print -u2 "aiblock: $_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT not found (run 'chezmoi apply' after a git pull)"
432	    return 1
433	  fi
434	  local histdump
435	  histdump=$(mktemp -t aiblock-hist.XXXXXX) || {
436	    print -u2 "aiblock: mktemp failed"
437	    return 1
438	  }
439	  # fc -ln -30: last 30 entries, no numbering. Trailing newline per entry.
440	  fc -ln -30 > "$histdump" 2>/dev/null
441	  AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP="$histdump" uv run --script "$_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT" "$@"
442	  local rc=$?
443	  rm -f "$histdump"
444	  return $rc
445	}

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: deep-merge a managed overlay into ~/.codex/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: Codex CLI rewrites this file at runtime, adding per-project trust
5	# (`[projects."<absolute-path>"]`) and marketplace paths
6	# (`[marketplaces.<id>]`) that are machine-specific. Tracking the whole file
7	# would create constant diff and bake one machine's paths into another's apply.
8	# We enforce only stable preferences (model, personality, [features],
9	# [plugins.*]) and round-trip the live machine state untouched.
10	#
11	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints
12	# the new contents on stdout. The merge runs in a small Python program because:
13	#   - jq doesn't speak TOML.
14	#   - mikefarah/yq's TOML emitter collapses nested tables into inline
15	#     `{ ... }` syntax and fails to quote keys with special characters
16	#     (e.g. `github@openai-curated`), producing invalid TOML on round-trip.
17	#   - Python 3.11+ ships `tomllib` built-in for reads; the inline writer below
18	#     handles the small schema this file uses (scalars, nested string-key
19	#     tables, no arrays-of-tables) and quotes every table key for safety.
20	#
21	# Merge precedence (later wins):
22	#   1. Stripped live (everything except [projects] and [marketplaces.*]).
23	#   2. Managed overlay (this script's $overlay heredoc).
24	#   3. Machine-local state ([projects.*], [marketplaces.*]) re-attached
25	#      verbatim so per-project trust survives an overlay churn.
26	#
27	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml
28	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (Linuxbrew/cargo-installed in the base ansible
29	# role; standard on macOS), which fetches a managed Python ≥ 3.11 if the host
30	# system python is older — guaranteeing built-in `tomllib`. Falls back to
31	# system `python3`, then to a no-op pass-through, so a fresh-bootstrap host
32	# without uv yet doesn't fail this modify_ script.
33	set -eu
34	
35	overlay=$(cat <<'TOML'
36	{{ template "agents/codex.config.overlay.toml" . }}
37	TOML
38	)
39	
40	base=$(cat)
41	
42	# Pick the python invocation. uv guarantees ≥3.11 → tomllib always
43	# importable; system python3 may be older but the script's own ImportError
44	# handler passes the live file through untouched if so. `--no-project`
45	# stops uv from picking up the dotfiles repo's pyproject.toml. `--quiet`
46	# silences "Installed X" log noise on first run.
47	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
48	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --python '>=3.11' python -
49	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	  set -- python3 -
51	else
52	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; skipping merge" >&2
53	  printf '%s' "$base"
54	  exit 0
55	fi
56	
57	# Pass live file + overlay via env vars; emit merged TOML on stdout. If
58	# anything goes wrong (tomllib missing on Python <3.11, malformed live file),
59	# Python prints to stderr and exits non-zero -> chezmoi skips the file.
60	CODEX_LIVE="$base" CODEX_OVERLAY="$overlay" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63	
64	try:
65	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
66	except ModuleNotFoundError:
67	    try:
68	        import tomli as tomllib  # backport for Python 3.10 and below
69	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
70	        print(
71	            "modify_config.toml: tomllib unavailable (need Python 3.11+ or "
72	            "`pip install tomli`); skipping merge",
73	            file=sys.stderr,
74	        )
75	        sys.stdout.write(os.environ.get("CODEX_LIVE", ""))
76	        sys.exit(0)
77	
78	
79	def parse(text: str) -> dict:
80	    text = text.strip()
81	    if not text:
82	        return {}
83	    return tomllib.loads(text)
84	
85	
86	def deep_merge(base: dict, overlay: dict) -> dict:
87	    """Recursive dict merge; overlay wins on conflict. Non-dict overlay
88	    values replace base wholesale (lists are not concatenated)."""
89	    out = dict(base)
90	    for k, v in overlay.items():
91	        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
92	            out[k] = deep_merge(out[k], v)
93	        else:
94	            out[k] = v
95	    return out
96	
97	
98	def prune_reserved_builtin_providers(live: dict) -> None:
99	    """Remove invalid overrides for Codex built-in provider IDs.
100	
101	    Codex accepts `model_providers.openai.*` via one-off `-c` CLI overrides but
102	    rejects persisted config.toml files that override the reserved built-in
103	    `openai` provider. Removing the whole table repairs configs produced by
104	    the previous GFW retry experiment and any equivalent manual override.
105	    Custom provider IDs such as `openai-gfw` are left untouched.
106	    """
107	    providers = live.get("model_providers")
108	    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
109	        return
110	    providers.pop("openai", None)
111	    if not providers:
112	        del live["model_providers"]
113	
114	
115	def fmt_scalar(v) -> str:
116	    if isinstance(v, bool):
117	        return "true" if v else "false"
118	    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
119	        return repr(v)
120	    if isinstance(v, str):
121	        # Use basic-string with escaping. tomllib accepts both basic and
122	        # literal; basic is universal.
123	        return '"' + v.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'
124	    if isinstance(v, list):
125	        return "[" + ", ".join(fmt_scalar(x) for x in v) + "]"
126	    raise TypeError(f"unsupported scalar type for TOML emit: {type(v).__name__}")
127	
128	
129	def emit_table(prefix: str, table: dict, out: list[str]) -> None:
130	    """Emit a TOML table. `prefix` is the dotted header path (already quoted
131	    where needed); empty for root. Scalars come first, then nested tables."""
132	    scalars = {k: v for k, v in table.items() if not isinstance(v, dict)}
133	    sub = {k: v for k, v in table.items() if isinstance(v, dict)}
134	
135	    if prefix and (scalars or not sub):
136	        out.append(f"[{prefix}]")
137	    for k, v in scalars.items():
138	        out.append(f"{quote_key(k)} = {fmt_scalar(v)}")
139	    if scalars and sub:
140	        out.append("")
141	
142	    for k, v in sub.items():
143	        sub_prefix = f"{prefix}.{quote_key(k)}" if prefix else quote_key(k)
144	        emit_table(sub_prefix, v, out)
145	        out.append("")
146	
147	
148	def quote_key(k: str) -> str:
149	    """Quote any key that isn't a bare TOML key (alnum / `_` / `-` only).
150	    We over-quote rather than risk emitting invalid TOML for keys like
151	    `github@openai-curated` or absolute-path project keys."""
152	    if k and all(c.isalnum() or c in "_-" for c in k):
153	        return k
154	    return '"' + k.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
155	
156	
157	live = parse(os.environ.get("CODEX_LIVE", ""))
158	overlay = parse(os.environ.get("CODEX_OVERLAY", ""))
159	prune_reserved_builtin_providers(live)
160	
161	# Pull machine-local subtrees out before merge; re-attach last so they win.
162	state = {}
163	for key in ("projects", "marketplaces"):
164	    if key in live:
165	        state[key] = live.pop(key)
166	
167	merged = deep_merge(live, overlay)
168	merged = deep_merge(merged, state)
169	
170	lines: list[str] = []
171	emit_table("", merged, lines)
172	text = "\n".join(line for line in lines if line is not None).rstrip() + "\n"
173	sys.stdout.write(text)
174	PYEOF
175

11	# the new contents on stdout. `jq '. * $overlay'` does recursive object merge.

19	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role). On a fresh-box first
20	# apply, jq isn't yet installed; this script falls back to passing the live
21	# file through unchanged. See pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.

25	{{ template "agents/opencode.overlay.json" . }}
26	JSON

32	# Cold-start fallback: jq is installed by the `base` ansible role, which

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: hook-aware deep-merge of a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json.
4	#
5	# Why hook-aware? Claude Code rewrites this file at runtime AND CodeIsland
6	# (https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland, macOS notch HUD) auto-installs its
7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces
9	# arrays wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would
10	# silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and
11	# CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
12	#
13	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
14	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
15	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
16	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
17	# notify.sh while CodeIsland (or any other tool) freely manages its own
18	# parallel entries in the same event arrays.
19	#
20	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
21	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.
22	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role). On a fresh-box first
23	# apply, jq isn't yet installed; this script falls back to passing the live
24	# file through unchanged. See pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
25	#
26	# See: docs/tools/agent-overlays.md → "CodeIsland integration".
27	set -eu
28	
29	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
30	{
31	  "hooks": {
32	    "Notification": [
33	      {
34	        "matcher": "",
35	        "hooks": [
36	          {
37	            "type": "command",
38	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
39	          }
40	        ]
41	      }
42	    ],
43	    "Stop": [
44	      {
45	        "hooks": [
46	          {
47	            "type": "command",
48	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
49	          }
50	        ]
51	      }
52	    ]
53	  },
54	  "enabledPlugins": {
55	    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true,
56	    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true
57	  },
58	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
59	    "claude-hud": {
60	      "source": {
61	        "source": "github",
62	        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
63	      }
64	    }
65	  },
66	  "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true,
67	  "permissions": {
68	    "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"
69	  },
70	  "statusLine": {
71	    "type": "command",
72	    "command": "bash -c 'plugin_dir=$(ls -d \"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}\"/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); runtime=$(command -v bun 2>/dev/null || command -v node 2>/dev/null); [ -z \"$runtime\" ] && exit 0; rt=\"${runtime##*/}\"; if [ \"$rt\" = \"bun\" ]; then exec \"$runtime\" --env-file /dev/null \"${plugin_dir}src/index.ts\"; else exec \"$runtime\" \"${plugin_dir}dist/index.js\"; fi'"
73	  }
74	}
75	JSON
76	)
77	
78	base=$(cat)
79	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{}'
80	
81	# Cold-start fallback: jq is installed by the `base` ansible role, which
82	# runs AFTER this file-apply phase. Pass the live file through unchanged
83	# and warn — the next apply (after ansible) does the real merge.
84	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
85	  printf '%s\n' "modify_settings.json: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
86	  printf '%s' "$base"
87	  exit 0
88	fi
89	
90	# Hook-aware merge:
91	#   1. Compute non-hook portion of overlay (everything except .hooks).
92	#   2. Deep-merge that into base normally: base * overlay_no_hooks.
93	#   3. For each event in overlay.hooks, append entries whose .hooks[0].command
94	#      isn't already represented in the live event array (by exact-string
95	#      command match on .hooks[0].command). Live entries are preserved
96	#      verbatim, and new overlay entries are added at the end.
97	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" '
98	  . as $base
99	  | ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
100	  | ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
101	  | ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
102	  | $merged
103	  | .hooks = (
104	      ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
105	      | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
106	          $live_hooks;
107	          .[$ev.key] = (
108	            (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
109	            | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
110	            | $live_arr + (
111	                $ev.value
112	                | map(select(
113	                    (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
114	                    | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
115	                  ))
116	              )
117	          )
118	        )
119	    )
120	'
121

```text
1	# aicapture — AI review of past shell commands
2	
3	Capture a past shell command's block from tmux scrollback, pipe it to a coding-agent CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor Agent) in non-interactive mode, get back a fix or explanation. Advisory by default: agent prints suggestions, doesn't touch files.
4	
5	Built on [OSC 133 semantic prompts](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md) — the shell emits `A`/`C`/`D` line-attribute markers, tmux stores them, our helpers navigate by them. For background on how this compares to `thefuck`, Warp, `wut`, `tmuxai`, `atuin`, etc., see [instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md](../this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md).
6	
7	> **Why not Charm [`mods`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/mods)?** `mods` is a generic CLI LLM client. We deliberately route through the existing agent CLIs (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor Agent) instead, because they own the per-tool model selection, system prompts, tool permissions, and project context that `aifix` / `aiexplain` rely on. `aicapture` is a tmux-scrollback capture layer, not a model-routing layer; the agent CLIs already handle the routing. Auto-detection chain lives in `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`.
8	
9	## Quick start
10	
11	```sh
12	# Any command that produced useful output or an error…
13	cargo build --release
14	
15	# …is one keystroke away from a diagnose + fix:
16	aifix
17	```
18	
19	Output in your terminal:
20	
21	```
22	aifix ← block -1
23	⠋ claude haiku (json)…                                  # spinner while agent thinks
24	claude (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) | in=12 out=87 cache=(r:24402,w:12487) | cost=$0.0008 3812ms
25	
26	## Fix for `cargo build` error
27	
28	Your `Cargo.toml` is missing the `serde` dependency. Add:
29	
30	    [dependencies]
31	    serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
32	
33	Then re-run `cargo build --release`.
34	```
35	
36	Reply is rendered as Markdown via `glow` (auto-falls back to `bat --language=md`, then raw text if neither is installed).
37	
38	## Commands
39	
40	### Capture (no AI call)
41	
42	Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly) **and** copies it to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge (works over SSH). Defaults to N=1 (most recent); pass a positive integer for N-back lookback.
43	
44	| Command | Scope |
45	|---|---|
46	| `cpcmd [N]` | Nth-latest command's **input line** (from zsh history — works outside tmux too) |
47	| `cpout [N]` | Nth-latest command's **output** only (via tmux + OSC 133) |
48	| `cpblock [N]` | Nth-latest command's **full block**: prompt + input + output (Warp-style) |
49	
50	```sh
51	cpblock                          # last block → clipboard + stdout
52	cpblock 3                        # 3rd-latest
53	cpout 2 | tee /tmp/snapshot.log  # pipe output to file while also copying
54	cpcmd                            # just the command string (no output)
55	```
56	
57	### AI review
58	
59	Same positional `[N]` as the capture helpers, plus flags:
60	
61	| Command | Default prompt |
62	|---|---|
63	| `aifix [N]` | *"Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."* |
64	| `aiexplain [N]` | *"Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise."* |
65	
66	Both accept:
67	
68	- `-a AGENT` — `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` / `cursor-agent`. Default: auto-detect (first one found on `$PATH`).
69	- `-p PROMPT` — override the default prompt.
70	- `--raw` — skip glow/bat prettify; print the agent's raw Markdown text.
71	- `--no-meta` — suppress the stderr metadata line (model / tokens / cost / duration).
72	- `-h` / `--help` — print the full signature and current env-var values.
73	
74	```sh
75	aifix                               # last block, default fix prompt
76	aifix 3 -a opencode                 # 3rd-latest, force OpenCode
77	aifix -p "is this safe on prod?"    # custom prompt
78	aiexplain 2 --raw                   # no prettify
79	aifix --no-meta | tee /tmp/ans.md   # pipe-friendly
80	```
81	
82	### Interactive TUI
83	
84	```sh
85	aiblock
86	```
87	
88	Launches a [questionary](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary) + [rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich) TUI ([`scripts/aiblock.py`](../../scripts/aiblock.py)) that walks through:
89	
90	1. **Checkbox picker** over the last 20 commands. Space toggles, Enter confirms. Picking none defaults to "last block".
91	2. **Preview** — each selected block shown in its own rich panel (multi-select concatenates in chronological order with `--- Block -N ---` separators so the agent can tell the turns apart).
92	3. **Prompt edit** — default is the `aifix` fix-prompt; edit inline.
93	4. **Action** — one of:
94	   - *Print reply here* — rendered as Markdown in a rich panel with the metadata as subtitle.
95	   - *Copy reply to clipboard* — via tmux OSC 52 / pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy.
96	   - *Spawn new tmux window running `<agent>`* — opens a fresh interactive agent session with your selected blocks pre-loaded into tmux's `aiblock` paste-buffer. Pull via `prefix + =`.
97	
98	The TUI depends on `uv` (PEP 723 inline deps) — no separate install step required; first run populates the uv cache.
99	
100	## Non-tmux alternatives
101	
102	When you're not in tmux (VSCode integrated terminal, bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH session), `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` can't see scrollback — they depend on tmux's OSC 133 line attributes. Three Tier 1 wrappers cover the common cases without magic (no shell hooks, no PTY proxy, no `script(1)` wrapping — see [`backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md`](../../backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md) for why we reject those paths):
103	
104	| Command | Source of context | Typical use |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| `aifix-stdin` | whatever you pipe in | `tail -100 build.log \| aifix-stdin` |
107	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | runs `CMD`, tees stdout+stderr to a log, reviews | `aifix-run -- cargo build --release` |
108	| `aifix-rerun` | re-executes the previous shell command (confirm prompt) | `aifix-rerun` after a transient error |
109	
110	All three accept the same flags as `aifix` (`-a AGENT` / `-p PROMPT` / `--raw` / `--no-meta`). `aifix-rerun` adds `-y` to skip the "⚠ side effects" confirmation. Default prompt for each is the `aifix` "diagnose + fix"; use `-p "explain what happened"` if you want the explain behaviour.
111	
112	```sh
113	# stdin — compose with any producer
114	tail -200 /var/log/nginx/error.log | aifix-stdin
115	curl -sS https://weird.api/thing | aifix-stdin -p "what is this JSON telling me?"
116	aifix-stdin < /tmp/build-fail.log
117	
118	# run — capture a fresh invocation (double-run safe, no prior history needed)
119	aifix-run -- ls /missing
120	aifix-run -p "is this safe on prod?" -- ansible-playbook deploy.yml
121	
122	# rerun — thefuck-style, re-execute last cmd. Confirms by default.
123	mvn compile      # fails
124	aifix-rerun      # "⚠ side effects…  Proceed? [y/N]"
125	aifix-rerun -y   # skip confirm
126	```
127	
128	**isatty caveat** for `aifix-run`: teeing makes CMD's stdout a pipe, so TUI apps (vim, less, htop) render in degraded mode. Don't `aifix-run` an interactive tool — pipe its log file via `aifix-stdin` after the fact instead.
129	
130	**Side-effect warning** for `aifix-rerun`: re-running `rm`, `curl -X POST`, `git push`, migrations, etc. is dangerous. The confirmation prompt is there for a reason; don't `-y` without reading what will be re-executed.
131	
132	## Configuration
133	
134	Put any of these in `~/.zshrc`, a `99_local_*.zsh` override, or export them per-session:
135	
136	```sh
137	# Model per agent (auto-detected order: claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent)
138	export AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=haiku                              # alias or full name (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6)
139	export AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL=github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5  # provider/model format
140	export AICAP_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5-mini
141	export AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL=                                    # empty = cursor-agent picks
142	
143	# Output behaviour
144	export AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1   # 0 to mute the stderr "claude (...) | in=... cost=..." line
145	export AICAP_PRETTIFY=1        # 0 to always print raw Markdown (skip glow/bat)
146	export AICAP_SPINNER=1         # 0 to disable the stderr spinner animation
147	```
148	
149	Check current settings any time with `aifix --help`.
150	
151	Defaults are tuned for Haiku-class models — fast (~5s round-trip) and cheap (~$0.001/call with cache hits). If you want Opus/Sonnet for harder diagnoses, set `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet` either globally or per-invocation:
152	
153	```sh
154	AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet aifix 3
155	```
156	
157	## Requirements
158	
159	| What | For |
160	|---|---|
161	| `zsh` | All commands (cpcmd, aifix, etc. are zsh functions) |
162	| `tmux 3.3+` | `cpout` / `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` (scrollback navigation) |
163	| OSC 133 shell integration | The hook in `dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh` emits the A/C/D markers tmux needs. Run `exec zsh` after install so the hook fires in your current shell. |
164	| At least one coding-agent CLI | `claude` (recommended), `opencode`, `codex`, or `cursor-agent` — install via your usual channel |
165	| `glow` (optional) | Markdown prettify on agent replies |
166	| `bat` (optional) | Prettify fallback when `glow` isn't present |
167	| `jq` (optional) | Parses Claude's `--output-format json` for the metadata line (tokens / cost) |
168	| `uv` (optional) | Needed only for the `aiblock` TUI — installs its Python deps lazily |
169	
170	## Standalone setup (no chezmoi)
171	
172	If you don't want to adopt the whole dotfiles repo, grab these four files and source them from your `~/.zshrc`. They're self-contained apart from the listed optional tools above.
173	
174	```sh
175	REPO=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main
176	mkdir -p ~/.config/zsh/tools
177	
178	# Shell side: OSC 133 hook + cpblock family + aifix family
179	for f in 02_shell_integration.zsh 03_tmux_capture.zsh 04_ai_capture.zsh; do
180	  curl -fsSL "$REPO/dot_config/zsh/tools/$f" -o "$HOME/.config/zsh/tools/$f"
181	done
182	
183	# Optional TUI (needs uv)
184	mkdir -p ~/.local/share/aicapture
185	curl -fsSL "$REPO/scripts/aiblock.py" -o ~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py
186	chmod +x ~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py
187	
188	# Append to ~/.zshrc (or equivalent)
189	cat >> ~/.zshrc <<'EOF'
190	for f in ~/.config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh \
191	         ~/.config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh \
192	         ~/.config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh; do
193	  [[ -r "$f" ]] && source "$f"
194	done
195	EOF
196	
197	# Reload
198	exec zsh
199	```
200	
201	The `aiblock` shell function resolves the TUI path via `chezmoi source-path`; if you're not on chezmoi, edit the `aiblock()` function in `04_ai_capture.zsh` to point at `~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py` instead:
202	
203	```zsh
204	# replace the chezmoi source-path block with:
205	_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT="$HOME/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py"
206	```
207	
208	### Read source on GitHub
209	
210	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — OSC 133 precmd/preexec hooks (A marker embedded in `$PROMPT` via `%{...%}` — see [`pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md) for why)
211	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh) — cpout / cpcmd / cpblock + tmux copy-mode chain helpers
212	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh) — aifix / aiexplain / aiblock wrappers, agent dispatch, spinner
213	- [`scripts/aiblock.py`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/scripts/aiblock.py) — Python TUI (PEP 723 inline deps)
214	
215	## Troubleshooting
216	
217	### `cpblock returned empty` / `aifix ← block -1` then nothing
218	
219	Your current shell was started before the hook was installed. The precmd/preexec hooks that emit OSC 133 markers need to be registered via `add-zsh-hook`, which only happens when `02_shell_integration.zsh` is sourced. Fix:
220	
221	```sh
222	exec zsh                                             # reload shell in place
223	echo $precmd_functions | tr ' ' '\n' | grep osc133   # verify
224	# expected: _osc133_precmd
225	```
226	
227	If `exec zsh` doesn't help, open a fresh tmux window — some terminal states don't propagate cleanly through `exec`.
228	
229	### `aiblock`: "Shell history is empty — no commands to pick from"
230	
231	Should no longer happen after commit `3993b7b`. If it does, the zsh wrapper that dumps history via `fc -ln -30` isn't running. Verify:
232	
233	```sh
234	which aiblock     # should show the function from 04_ai_capture.zsh
235	type aiblock      # should show the fc-dump logic
236	```
237	
238	Workaround: the TUI also falls back to parsing `$HISTFILE` directly, so `HISTFILE=~/.zsh_history aiblock` works even if the wrapper is broken.
239	
240	### Metadata line shows `claude (?)` instead of the model
241	
242	`jq` failed to find `.modelUsage | keys | first` in Claude's JSON output. Either `jq` is out of date (install latest) or Claude CLI changed its JSON shape. Set `AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=0` to bypass until fixed.
243	
244	### Spinner doesn't appear / doesn't disappear
245	
246	Spinner auto-skips when stderr isn't a tty. If you're redirecting with `2>/tmp/err` or piping through `tee` you won't see it — by design.
247

```text
1	# Coding-agent CLI overlays (Cursor / OpenCode / Codex)
2	
3	This repo manages the *global* config files of three coding-agent CLIs via chezmoi `modify_` overlays:
4	
5	| CLI | Live file | Source script | Merge engine |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| Cursor | `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` | [`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl`](../../dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
8	| OpenCode (server/runtime) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
9	| OpenCode (TUI) | `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
10	| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) | Python `tomllib` + inline emitter |
11	
12	Overlay payloads live under [`.chezmoitemplates/agents/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/) and are sourced via `{{ template ... }}` includes so the merge logic can be tested independently of overlay contents.
13	
14	> **Why not Charm [`crush`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush)?** `crush` is Charm's own agentic coding CLI. Adding it would mean a fifth overlay (binary + auth + per-project trust + marketplace state), and the cost-of-ownership of each agent overlay is non-trivial — every CLI that rewrites its own config file at runtime needs a hook-aware merger, TOML/JSON round-tripper, and presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. The existing trio (Cursor / OpenCode / Codex, plus Claude Code via `dot_claude/modify_settings.json`) already covers the practical agent-CLI design space. If you want to evaluate `crush`, the add-a-fifth-CLI pattern is: install in `dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`, add `dot_crush/modify_<config>` plus `.chezmoitemplates/agents/crush.overlay.<json|toml>`, then optionally wire into the `04_ai_capture.zsh` agent-detection chain.
15	
16	## Why `modify_` and not full file management
17	
18	All three CLIs **rewrite their config file at runtime** to record machine-local state: auth tokens, telemetry IDs, per-project trust grants, marketplace registrations with absolute paths, plugin-cache hashes, last-used provider hints, etc. Tracking the whole file as managed content would:
19	
20	1. Leak secrets (`authInfo`, `auth.json` content) into the dotfiles repo.
21	2. Bake one machine's absolute paths (`/Users/me/.codex/.tmp/...`) into another machine's apply.
22	3. Produce constant `chezmoi diff` noise as the CLI churns the file.
23	
24	The `modify_` overlay model deep-merges only the keys we explicitly enforce; everything else passes through verbatim.
25	
26	## What each overlay enforces
27	
28	### Cursor — [`agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json)
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "editor": { "vimMode": true }
33	}
34	```
35	
36	- `editor.vimMode = true` — universal preference; sibling `editor.fontSize` etc. survive the deep merge.
37	- **`permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays are intentionally NOT in the overlay.** `jq '. * $overlay'` replaces arrays wholesale at the same key path, so listing any entries here would clobber the user's live machine-specific allow-list on every `chezmoi apply`. Manage those per machine via the live file directly, or move to a `--argjson allow $merged` array-union approach if you ever need a shared baseline.
38	
39	### OpenCode — [`agents/opencode.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.overlay.json)
40	
41	```json
42	{
43	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
44	  "autoupdate": true,
45	  "default_agent": "build",
46	  "small_model": "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini",
47	  "agent": { "title": { "reasoningEffort": "low" } },
48	  "provider": {
49	    "github-copilot": {
50	      "options": { "timeout": 600000 }
51	    }
52	  }
53	}
54	```
55	
56	- `$schema` — keeps editors aware of the schema for autocomplete.
57	- `autoupdate = true` — let the CLI self-update.
58	- `default_agent = "build"` — primary agent on TUI/CLI startup. Override per-session via `--agent` or the picker.
59	- `small_model = "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini"` — cheap model for title generation, summarisation, and other lightweight calls. Avoids billing Claude Opus quota for trivial tasks. Pairs with `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"`.
60	- `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"` — cheap completions for short title generation; sibling `agent.*` entries (per-agent provider, model overrides) survive.
61	- `provider.github-copilot.options.timeout = 600000` (10 min) — request-level timeout. Default is 5 min; bumped to give long Claude Opus generations more room before the SDK aborts the whole call. **Note**: `chunkTimeout` is intentionally NOT set here, see [docs/tools/opencode.md → Claude Opus stream stall](opencode.md#claude-opus-stream-stall-on-github-copilot) for the rationale (upstream bug [anomalyco/opencode#20466](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20466) — SSE-chunk-timeout errors aren't retried, so setting `chunkTimeout` would convert silent hangs into hard failures with no recovery).
62	
63	### OpenCode TUI — [`agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json)
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
68	  "keybinds": { "leader": "ctrl+x" },
69	  "mouse": true,
70	  "diff_style": "auto",
71	  "scroll_acceleration": { "enabled": true }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	The TUI lives in a **separate file** from server/runtime config: `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` with its own schema `https://opencode.ai/tui.json`. See upstream docs:
76	
77	- [Config → TUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#tui) — file location, schema URL, precedence
78	- [TUI → Configure → Options](https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/#options) — per-key semantics
79	
80	Key-by-key rationale:
81	
82	- `$schema = "https://opencode.ai/tui.json"` — TUI schema (different from `opencode.json`'s `config.json` schema). Lets editors validate + autocomplete.
83	- `keybinds.leader = "ctrl+x"` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Declaring it ensures muscle memory + the `<leader>` references in [docs/keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/) survive any future upstream default change. The other ~80 keybind defaults are intentionally NOT pinned here — they stay tracking upstream so new actions added by OpenCode become available without overlay churn.
84	- `mouse = true` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Trades terminal-native select-to-copy for OpenCode's in-TUI mouse support (scroll, click).
85	- `diff_style = "auto"` — adapts diff layout to terminal width (vs `"stacked"` which forces single-column). Pinning the upstream default makes intent explicit.
86	- `scroll_acceleration.enabled = true` — macOS-style smooth/accelerated scrolling. Per upstream docs this **takes precedence over and overrides** `scroll_speed`, so we deliberately omit `scroll_speed` from the overlay (setting both would mislead — the latter would be silently ignored).
87	
88	What's intentionally NOT in the TUI overlay:
89	
90	- `theme` — left unset so OpenCode's auto light/dark detection stays in effect (matches the system theme just like `ghostty` and the `tmux` theme switcher in this repo).
91	- Individual `keybinds.*` entries beyond `leader` — see above. fzf's shell-level `Ctrl+T` and OpenCode's `variant_cycle = ctrl+t` do not collide because they live in disjoint namespaces (shell prompt vs OpenCode TUI).
92	- `username_toggle` / `tips_toggle` / `display_thinking` — these are persisted by the TUI's `/help` customisation panel at runtime. Pinning them in the overlay would clobber the user's last in-app choice on every `chezmoi apply`, same anti-pattern as managing `plugin` paths or auth tokens.
93	- `scroll_speed` — see `scroll_acceleration.enabled` above; OpenCode ignores `scroll_speed` whenever acceleration is enabled.
94	
95	### Codex — [`agents/codex.config.overlay.toml`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml)
96	
97	```toml
98	personality = "pragmatic"
99	model = "gpt-5.4"
100	model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
101	
102	[features]
103	codex_hooks = true
104	unified_exec = true
105	shell_snapshot = true
106	steer = true
107	multi_agent = true
108	
109	[plugins."github@openai-curated"]
110	enabled = true
111	
112	[plugins."google-drive@openai-curated"]
113	enabled = true
114	
115	[plugins."computer-use@openai-bundled"]
116	enabled = true
117	```
118	
119	- Top-level model + reasoning preferences.
120	- `[features]` — opt into the experimental flags this user always wants on.
121	- `[plugins."<id>".enabled]` — curated plugin set; user-installed plugins appear under their own `[plugins."..."]` blocks and are preserved by the deep merge.
122	
123	The overlay intentionally does **not** persist `[model_providers.openai]` overrides. Codex CLI accepts those knobs as one-off `-c` overrides, but rejects `config.toml` files that override reserved built-in provider IDs such as `openai`. The modify script removes stale `[model_providers.openai]` tables left by earlier experiments while preserving custom provider IDs such as `[model_providers.openai-gfw]`.
124	
125	## What is intentionally NOT managed
126	
127	| File / subtree | CLI | Why |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| `~/.cursor/{authInfo,auth*,privacyCache,statsigBootstrap,version,hasChangedDefaultModel,...}` | Cursor | Auth + telemetry; runtime-only. |
130	| `~/.cursor/{extensions,plugins,projects,worktrees,workers,browser-logs,chats,plans,prompt_history.json,argv.json,ide_state.json,agent-cli-state.json,ai-tracking,mcp.json,skills-cursor}` | Cursor | CLI-managed state, per-project, machine-local. |
131	| `~/.config/opencode/{node_modules,package.json,bun.lock,package-lock.json,plugins/}` | OpenCode | Node runtime + locally-installed plugin source trees. |
132	| `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` keys outside the TUI overlay (`theme`, `keybinds.*` other than `leader`, `username_toggle`, `tips_toggle`, `display_thinking`, `scroll_speed`) | OpenCode | TUI runtime customisation panel persists user choices here; overlay only pins stable preferences. |
133	| `~/.codex/auth.json` | Codex | OpenAI auth token. **Never** check in. |

135	| `~/.codex/[marketplaces.<id>]` | Codex | Marketplace registrations with absolute `source = "/Users/.../.codex/.tmp/..."` paths. **Round-tripped**. |
136	| `~/.codex/{installation_id,history.jsonl,session_index.jsonl,sessions/,logs_*.sqlite*,state_*.sqlite,cache/,tmp/,log/,sqlite/,memories/,vendor_imports/,shell_snapshots/,models_cache.json,plugins/,skills/,rules/,ambient-suggestions/,version.json,AGENTS.md,.tmp/}` | Codex | Sessions, logs, sqlite, plugin/skills directories, machine-local notes. |
137	
138	The `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` presence-gates the entire `~/.cursor/`, `~/.codex/`, and `~/.config/opencode/` trees with a `stat` check so uninstalled CLIs never produce phantom directories.
139	
140	## How the Codex TOML merge works
141	
142	`jq` doesn't speak TOML and `mikefarah/yq`'s TOML emitter produces invalid output for keys with special characters (e.g. `github@openai-curated`). The Codex `modify_` script uses Python instead:
143	
144	1. Read live file into a `dict` via `tomllib` (Python 3.11+ built-in; `tomli` fallback for 3.10).
145	2. Pop `[projects]` and `[marketplaces]` subtrees into `state`.
146	3. Read overlay TOML into a `dict`.
147	4. Deep-merge: `live_minus_state <- overlay <- state`. Argument order is merge precedence (later wins). State wins last so per-project trust never gets clobbered by an overlay churn.
148	5. Emit TOML via a 30-line writer that quotes all non-bareword keys (handles `github@openai-curated` and `/Users/me/foo`-style project keys).
149	
150	The script falls through to passing the live file untouched if `python3` or `tomllib`/`tomli` are missing; chezmoi will skip the file for that apply.
151	
152	## OpenCode legacy `config.json` migration
153	
154	OpenCode docs now recommend `opencode.json` as the canonical filename, but installations from before that change use `config.json`. The repo manages only the modern filename; a one-shot script handles the migration:
155	
156	- [`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`](../../run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl) runs once per source-state hash, before chezmoi deploys files. It:
157	  1. No-ops if `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is absent.
158	  2. If only the legacy file exists: rename it to `opencode.json`.
159	  3. If both exist: deep-merge legacy into modern (modern wins on conflict, since it's presumed newer), then delete legacy.
160	
161	After this script runs, the `modify_opencode.json` overlay enforces the managed keys on the unified file. The legacy filename never reappears because OpenCode itself only writes `opencode.json` going forward.
162	
163	The migration script can be removed from the repo a few months after rollout (once all machines have run `chezmoi apply` at least once); it is idempotent and a no-op on fresh machines, so it's safe to leave indefinitely.
164	
165	## Refresh recipe
166	
167	To change what an overlay enforces, edit the corresponding `.chezmoitemplates/agents/<cli>.overlay.{json,toml}` file. Do **not** `chezmoi add` the live config — that would strip the `modify_` prefix and overwrite the script with the runtime file (which contains your secrets).
168	
169	To pull a new key from the live file into the overlay (e.g. you changed a Cursor permission you want shared):
170	
171	```bash
172	# 1. Inspect the live file
173	jq . ~/.cursor/cli-config.json
174	
175	# 2. Edit the overlay JSON / TOML and add the key
176	$EDITOR .chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json
177	
178	# 3. Verify the rendered modify_ script outputs what you expect
179	chezmoi execute-template < dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl > /tmp/m.sh
180	chmod +x /tmp/m.sh
181	cat ~/.cursor/cli-config.json | /tmp/m.sh
182	
183	# 4. Apply
184	chezmoi apply
185	```
186	
187	## Tests
188	
189	[`tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`](../../tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats) covers:
190	
191	- Each overlay enforces its declared keys.
192	- Live runtime keys outside the overlay are preserved verbatim.
193	- Codex `[projects.*]` and `[marketplaces.*]` round-trip unchanged (the round-trip property is the load-bearing invariant — break it and machines start clobbering each other's per-project trust).
194	- The modify_ scripts are idempotent (running output through the script again produces the same output).
195	- The OpenCode migration handles all three input states: legacy-only, both-present, neither-present.
196	- The Claude hook-aware merger (see next section): notify.sh added when missing; CodeIsland entries preserved; idempotency on re-apply; non-hook deep-merge preserves user siblings.
197	
198	Run with `just bats` (or directly: `bats tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`).
199	
200	## CodeIsland integration (macOS-only)
201	
202	[CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) is a macOS notch-area HUD (positioning analogous to [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar)) that surfaces real-time activity from 11+ coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, AntiGravity, Trae, Qoder, Factory, CodeBuddy, Kimi). It works by injecting per-CLI hook entries that fire `~/.codeisland/codeisland-bridge` (or `codeisland-hook.sh`), which streams events over a Unix socket at `/tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock` to the SwiftUI app.
203	
204	### Why macOS-only
205	
206	- Swift app, requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.
207	- The notch UI assumes a MacBook display geometry.
208	- Distribution is via brew cask (`wxtsky/tap`) or `.dmg`.
209	
210	There is no Linux fallback — the wire format depends on the macOS-specific bridge binary and socket path. We deliberately install nothing for CodeIsland on Linux and skip all related concerns there.
211	
212	### Install
213	
214	The `codeisland` cask is added in [`dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](../../dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) inside the `{{ if .installAiDesktopApps }}` block alongside the other agent desktop apps:
215	
216	```ruby
217	tap "wxtsky/tap"
218	cask "codeisland"
219	```
220	
221	### How we coexist with the app
222	
223	CodeIsland's settings panel calls itself "Auto hook install" with "auto-repair and version tracking" — meaning the **app actively writes and re-writes** hook entries into each detected CLI's config on every launch. Two coexistence patterns:
224	
225	> **Note (2026-04-25)**: CodeIsland v1.0.23 dropped `ExitPlanMode` from the default `HookServer.autoApproveTools` whitelist — plan-mode exit now prompts a real confirm dialog, and Settings → Behavior → "Auto-approve Tools" lets users toggle individual tools. See [`pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md`](../../pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md). Our merger continues to *additively* preserve every CodeIsland hook entry — no subtractive logic was added, because the upstream fix is the right path and the `PermissionRequest` hook is now a legitimate input source for the notch popup, not a bypass mechanism.
226	
227	#### Pattern A — Sidecar files (always-ignored)
228	
229	CLIs whose hooks live in a dedicated sidecar (containing nothing but CodeIsland hooks) are simply unmanaged by chezmoi. Concretely:
230	
231	| File | CLI | Why unmanaged |
232	|------|-----|---------------|
233	| `~/.codex/hooks.json` | Codex | Pure CodeIsland sidecar (also extended by Superset's notify.sh in some setups, but that's installed by Superset, not us) |
234	| `~/.cursor/hooks.json` | Cursor | Same |
235	| `~/.copilot/hooks/codeisland.json` | GitHub Copilot CLI | Pure CodeIsland sidecar |
236	| `~/.gemini/settings.json` | Gemini CLI | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
237	| `~/.antigravity/settings.json` | AntiGravity (CLI, not the editor) | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
238	
239	These paths are added to [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) as **always-ignore** so accidentally running `chezmoi add ~/.codex/hooks.json` won't pull a CodeIsland-owned file into the source tree (which would clobber the app's runtime updates and create a ping-pong with its auto-installer).
240	
241	If you later want to manage non-hook prefs in `~/.gemini/settings.json` or `~/.antigravity/settings.json`, write a `modify_` overlay that follows the hook-aware pattern below — and remove the corresponding ignore line.
242	
243	#### Pattern B — Mixed files (hook-aware merger)
244	
245	Files where stable user prefs and CodeIsland hooks coexist need a smarter overlay. Currently the only such file is **`~/.claude/settings.json`** — Claude Code stores model selection, plugins, statusLine, and `permissions.defaultMode` in the same file as `hooks.<event>` arrays. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays wholesale: declaring a `hooks.Notification` entry in our overlay would silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply`, then CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong producing diff noise and broken integrations.
246	
247	[`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) solves this with a hook-aware merger:
248	
249	1. **Non-hook keys** (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, `permissions.defaultMode`, `statusLine`, …) deep-merge normally via `base * overlay_no_hooks`. Note: `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` is set deliberately to work around Claude Code resetting the active permission mode after every interactive prompt (`AskUserQuestion`, CodeIsland popup, remote-control inject); see [`pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md`](../../pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md). The deep-merge writes the `defaultMode` scalar without touching sibling `permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays — those remain machine-local.
250	2. **`hooks.<event>` arrays** are merged additively: for each event the overlay declares, append entries whose `.hooks[0].command` isn't already represented in the live array (string-equality match). Live entries are preserved verbatim, no entry is ever removed.
251	
252	The full filter (jq):
253	
254	```jq
255	. as $base
256	| ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
257	| ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
258	| ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
259	| $merged
260	| .hooks = (
261	    ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
262	    | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
263	        $live_hooks;
264	        .[$ev.key] = (
265	          (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
266	          | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
267	          | $live_arr + (
268	              $ev.value
269	              | map(select(
270	                  (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
271	                  | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
272	                ))
273	            )
274	        )
275	      )
276	  )
277	```
278	
279	Test coverage in `tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`:
280	
281	- `claude modify_settings: notify.sh added to empty hooks, codeisland entries preserved` — proves the additive append works without removing CodeIsland entries.
282	- `claude modify_settings: idempotent when notify.sh already present` — proves no duplicate appears on re-apply.
283	- `claude modify_settings: empty live file produces overlay-only output` — bootstrap on a fresh machine.
284	- `claude modify_settings: non-hook deep-merge preserves siblings` — proves user-added plugins/marketplaces survive.
285	
286	> **Sibling overlay**: `~/.claude/keybindings.json` is managed by a separate, simpler `modify_` script — [`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json). It is NOT hook-aware (CodeIsland doesn't write to keybindings.json). See [Claude Code keybindings](claude-code-keybindings.md) for its design, the `chat:cycleMode`-only mode-jump limitation, and how to add personal binding overrides.
287

Could be extended to also fire `apprise --tag webhook` for remote chat-app delivery (Slack, Discord, Telegram, …) using URLs configured in `~/.config/apprise/apprise.yaml`. ```text
1	# Non-tmux output capture for aifix / aiexplain
2	
3	**Status**: P2 deferred (Tier 2); **P3 rejected** (Tier 3)
4	**Effort**: M (Tier 2) / XL-won't-do (Tier 3)
5	**Related**: [`TODO.md`](../TODO.md) · [`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`](../dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh) · [`docs/tools/aicapture.md`](../docs/tools/aicapture.md) · [`docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md`](../docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	**2026-04**: shipped `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `cpblock` / `aiblock` which all require tmux because they lean on OSC 133 line-attribute tracking in tmux's grid. Users in non-tmux environments (VSCode integrated terminal, bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH where starting tmux is inconvenient) can use `cpcmd` (shell history — input only) but not the output-level capture.
10	
11	Tier 1 shipped in the same batch: `aifix-stdin` / `aifix-run` / `aifix-rerun` — three zero-magic wrappers where the user explicitly provides the context (stdin / fresh invocation / re-execute). They cover the common cases but require the user to remember which one to pick.
12	
13	This entry records what a more-transparent "Tier 2" or "Tier 3" would look like, and — more importantly — **why we're not building them**, so future-us doesn't spend a weekend rediscovering these trade-offs.
14	
15	## Investigation
16	
17	From [`docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md`](../docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md), the four known strategies for "bound the previous command":
18	
19	1. **Shell history file** — only sees the command string, no output. What `thefuck` does; works fine for typos, useless for runtime errors.
20	2. **Shell hooks + OSC 133** — what we do. Needs a terminal multiplexer or OSC-133-aware terminal to store the markers; tmux consumes the marker bytes into grid line attributes and doesn't re-emit them from `capture-pane -pe`.
21	3. **tmux `capture-pane`** — what `wut` / `tmuxai` / our `cpblock` do. Fails outside tmux.
22	4. **PTY proxy** — `butterfish` / Warp. The AI shell IS the terminal.
23	
24	No one has a "automatic, no shell integration, no PTY proxy, no tmux" solution — it's a physics limit, not an engineering gap.
25	
26	### thefuck's approach (for comparison)
27	
28	```zsh
29	# thefuck/shells/zsh.py fuck() alias snippet
30	TF_HISTORY="$(fc -ln -10)"
31	TF_CMD=$(thefuck THEFUCK_ARGUMENT_PLACEHOLDER "$@") && eval $TF_CMD
32	```
33	
34	Then Python:
35	
36	```python
37	proc = Popen(script, shell=True, env=..., stderr=STDOUT, stdout=PIPE)
38	output = proc.communicate(timeout=settings.wait_command)[0]
39	```
40	
41	**It re-runs the command** to get stdout+stderr — exactly what our Tier 1 `aifix-rerun` does, but with less ceremony. Cost: `rm`, `curl -X POST`, `cargo build` get executed twice.
42	
43	### atuin's choice to NOT store output
44	
45	[atuin](https://github.com/atuinsh/atuin) is the closest "serious shell-history database" project. It stores command, exit code, duration, cwd, host — [explicitly not output](https://blog.atuin.sh/) because output is typically large and rarely needed later. If we went further we'd be reinventing their design space; better to compose with atuin than compete.
46	
47	## Options considered
48	
49	| Option | Pros | Cons |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| **Tier 1 (SHIPPED)** — `aifix-stdin` / `aifix-run` / `aifix-rerun` | Zero magic, composes with any pipe, user has full control | User must remember to prefix / pipe; no "just works after a failed command" reflex |
52	| **Tier 2 — zsh preexec/precmd tee redirect** | Transparent: user just runs commands, `aifix` finds the output automatically | `exec > >(tee FILE)` breaks `isatty(1)` for the running command → TUI apps (vim, less, htop, ncurses) render in degraded mode; ZLE timing is fragile (same family as the [OSC 133 A-marker pitfall](../pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md)); `/tmp` fills up if not capped |
53	| **Tier 3a — wrap every shell in `script(1)`** | PTY emulation keeps `isatty(1)` truthy, so TUIs still work | `script(1)` has job-control quirks with zsh (fg/bg misbehave), some tools detect they're "inside script" and change behaviour, log files pile up, you end up with layers like `zsh inside script inside tmux inside terminal` which is hell to debug |
54	| **Tier 3b — PTY proxy (butterfish-style)** | Richest context (every keystroke + every output byte) | Effectively rewriting our own terminal; gives up portability; puts us in the Warp/butterfish product category which this repo intentionally isn't |
55	
56	## Current blocker / open questions
57	
58	**Deferred, not blocked.** Tier 1 (shipped) handles the common cases. Tier 2 needs research on keeping `isatty(1)` truthy under tee (maybe a PTY-pair shim? Maybe `zpty` from `zsh/zpty` module?). Tier 3 is a deliberate "no" — see Decision below.
59	
60	Re-evaluate Tier 2 if:
61	
62	- Three or more users (or recurring personal workflows) report needing output capture in non-tmux sessions specifically, AND the Tier 1 commands aren't good enough;
63	- Someone finds a clean way to keep `isatty(1)` truthy during transparent tee, maybe via `zsh/zpty` module or a custom `mkfifo` dance;
64	- The TUI-app-breakage testing burden becomes tractable (a small curated whitelist turns out to be 95% sufficient).
65	
66	## Decision (2026-04)
67	
68	- **Tier 1 shipped** in the same batch as this backlog entry.
69	- **Tier 2 deferred** — the effort is "Medium" (maybe 4-8 hours of plumbing) but the *testing* burden is L-to-XL: we'd need to validate against every TUI the user runs (vim, nvim, less, htop, btop, lazygit, fzf, tldr, systemctl status, journalctl -f, tmux-itself…) to make sure we aren't breaking them. Benefit is limited to the subset of users who (a) work without tmux daily AND (b) hit the "forgot to pipe" reflex often enough that Tier 1 isn't good enough. Low ROI.
70	- **Tier 3 rejected.** Matches the "What we intentionally don't do and shouldn't start" section of [`instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md`](../docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md). Both variants require re-architecting this repo around a shell-subsuming wrapper, giving up portability and adding a permanent extra layer. "Just use tmux" is this repo's house style — we already have the tmux invariant (see [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) → tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu), so asking output-capture users to do the same isn't a new constraint.
71	
72	## References
73	
74	- thefuck's eval-alias approach: [nvbn/thefuck/shells/zsh.py](https://github.com/nvbn/thefuck/blob/master/thefuck/shells/zsh.py)
75	- butterfish PTY proxy design post: [pbbakkum.com/blog/20230927](https://pbbakkum.com/blog/20230927/)
76	- atuin's decision to not capture output: [blog.atuin.sh](https://blog.atuin.sh/)
77	- Related pitfall about ZLE timing: [`pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md`](../pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md)
78	- Prior art survey: [`docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md`](../docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md)

101	def list_recent_commands(n: int = 20) -> list[HistoryEntry]:
102	    """Return the last `n` shell commands as HistoryEntry(N, cmd).
103	
104	    Reads $AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP (written by the zsh `aiblock` wrapper via
105	    `fc -ln -30`) — a `zsh -ic fc …` subshell does NOT see the current
106	    shell's in-memory history, and `fc -R` from HISTFILE misses commands
107	    that haven't been flushed yet. The env-passed dump is the only
108	    reliable source for "what did the USER just run".
109	
110	    Falls back to parsing $HISTFILE directly if the dump env var isn't
111	    set (e.g. someone ran the script without the wrapper).
112	
113	    Returned list is ordered most-recent-first, with `.n` matching what
114	    cpblock/cpcmd/cpout expect as their positional N arg.
115	    """
116	    dump_path = os.environ.get("AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP")
117	    lines: list[str] = []
118	    if dump_path and os.path.isfile(dump_path):
119	        with open(dump_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
120	            lines = [ln.strip() for ln in f if ln.strip()]
121	    else:
122	        # Fallback: parse HISTFILE directly.
123	        histfile = os.environ.get("HISTFILE") or os.path.expanduser("~/.zsh_history")
124	        if os.path.isfile(histfile):
125	            with open(histfile, encoding="latin-1", errors="replace") as f:
126	                raw = f.readlines()
127	            for raw_ln in raw[-n * 3:]:  # last 3N raw lines (covers line continuations)
128	                s = raw_ln.rstrip("\n").strip()
129	                if not s:
130	                    continue
131	                # EXTENDED_HISTORY format: ": TIMESTAMP:DURATION;CMD"
132	                if s.startswith(": "):
133	                    parts = s.split(";", 1)
134	                    if len(parts) == 2:
135	                        s = parts[1]
136	                lines.append(s)
137	    # Take the last n, reverse so index 1 == most recent.
138	    lines = lines[-n:]
139	    return [HistoryEntry(n=i, command=cmd) for i, cmd in enumerate(reversed(lines), start=1)]

1	# aisuggest — prompt-time NL→shell ghost text via the existing _aiagent_invoke
2	# layer. Press the trigger (Alt+; default) to translate the current BUFFER from
3	# natural language into a single shell command, shown as ghost text. Tab or →
4	# accepts; any other keypress dismisses.
5	#
6	# Integrates with 04_ai_capture.zsh (_aiagent_invoke / _aiagent_autodetect) so
7	# the same agent autodetect (claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent) and the
8	# same AICAP_*_MODEL defaults apply. No API key needed when claude / opencode /
9	# codex / cursor-agent CLIs are authenticated.
10	#
11	# Env-var defaults (set in ~/.zshrc.adhoc or ~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh to
12	# override; do not edit this file):
13	#
14	#   AISUGGEST_KEY              default: ^[;            (Alt+;)
15	#   AISUGGEST_AGENT            default: empty          (autodetect at invoke)
16	#   AISUGGEST_MODEL            default: empty          (use AICAP_*_MODEL)
17	#   AISUGGEST_HIGHLIGHT        default: fg=8           (region_highlight style)
18	#   AISUGGEST_PROMPT_OVERRIDE  default: empty          (replace built-in prompt)
19	#   AISUGGEST_DEBUG            default: 0              (1 = log every widget step
20	#                                                       to $AISUGGEST_LOG;
21	#                                                       runtime-toggleable)
22	#   AISUGGEST_LOG              default: /tmp/aisuggest.log
23	#
24	# Debugging:
25	#   `aisuggest "<text>"`              CLI form — same pipeline as the widget,
26	#                                     prints the suggestion to stdout.
27	#   `aisuggest --debug "<text>"`      Also prints raw / sanitized / final to
28	#                                     stderr layer-by-layer.
29	#   `export AISUGGEST_DEBUG=1`        Trace every widget step to $AISUGGEST_LOG.
30	#
31	# Architecture + design notes: docs/tools/zsh-inline-ai.md
32	#
33	# Roadmap (full rationale + upstream pointers in the doc above, "Roadmap" section):
34	#   1. Low-latency claude flag profile — bypass _aiagent_invoke for `agent==claude`,
35	#      shell out with `--no-session-persistence --effort low --no-chrome --tools ""
36	#      --setting-sources "" --system-prompt "$sys" "$user_input"`. ~1.5x faster.
37	#      Upstream ref: providers/claude-code.zsh.
38	#   2. Pass system prompt via `--system-prompt` flag instead of concatenating into
39	#      the user message. Tighter rule-following.
40	#   3. Async via `zle -F <fd>`. Currently we block the prompt during the agent call.
41	#      A non-blocking flow (background agent → FD watcher → render-on-arrival) lets
42	#      the user keep typing while the suggestion renders.
43	#   4. Direct API providers (anthropic / openai / gemini via curl + jq) for users
44	#      without any of the four CLIs installed. Pair with a key-retrieval-command
45	#      env var (1Password / pass / GNOME Keyring / AWS Secrets Manager).
46	#   5. Sanitize regression test (port upstream's test-sanitize.sh — crafted ANSI /
47	#      control-char payloads → assert _aisuggest_sanitize strips them).
48	#   6. Per-agent model env vars (AISUGGEST_CLAUDE_MODEL, AISUGGEST_OPENCODE_MODEL, …)
49	#      so users can pin different models per agent without re-exporting on switch.
50	
51	# Prevent double-load (creates nested widget wrappers)
52	(( ${+functions[_aisuggest_widget]} )) && return
53

56	command -v curl &>/dev/null || return 0
57	command -v jq   &>/dev/null || return 0
