# Plan — Add `http` agent + `AICAP_AGENT` override to ai-capture

## Context

`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh` powers `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` (one-shot agent review of terminal output). It currently auto-detects one of four installed CLIs in fixed order (`claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent`) and routes the prompt through the matched CLI. This locks the user out of two cheap/free routes:

- **OpenRouter free models** (`openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free` etc.) — useful when the local host has no agent CLI installed but does have `curl` + an API key.
- **Local Ollama** (`http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions`) — useful for privacy-sensitive output and offline / air-gapped hosts.

We also have no clean way to force a specific agent without typing `-a <agent>` on every call, even when several CLIs are installed.

The change: add a new `http` agent type that talks an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint directly (covers both OpenRouter and Ollama since they share the schema), and add an `AICAP_AGENT` env var that overrides the auto-detect chain. Auto-detect order stays unchanged. The `http` agent is opt-in via `AICAP_AGENT=http` (it has nothing to probe on PATH).

## Design

### New env vars

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AICAP_AGENT` | `<unset>` | If set, skip auto-detect and use this agent. One of: `claude` `opencode` `codex` `cursor-agent` `http`. Per-call `-a` flag still wins. |
| `AICAP_HTTP_URL` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` | Full chat-completions URL. Set to `http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions` for Ollama. |
| `AICAP_HTTP_MODEL` | `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free` | Model name as expected by the endpoint. |
| `AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY` | `${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}` | Bearer token. Empty = no `Authorization` header (Ollama works this way). |

`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` fallback is intentional — OpenRouter docs already use that name and many users will have it set in their secrets.

### Code changes

#### 1. `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`

- Add the four `:` defaults (lines ~28-34 block) for the new vars except `AICAP_AGENT` (which must stay unset to mean "auto").
- New `http` branch in `_aiagent_invoke()` (after `cursor-agent)` at line 161). Build JSON payload with `jq -n --arg m … --arg p …`, `curl -sS -X POST` with optional `Authorization` header, `jq` out `.choices[0].message.content`. Surface `.error.message` to stderr if present. Emit a metadata line (`http (<model>) | in=<n> out=<n>`) when `AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1`. Spinner label `http <model>…`.
- In the dispatchers (`_ai_capture_dispatch`, `aifix-stdin`, `aifix-run`), before the auto-detect call: `[[ -z "$agent" && -n "$AICAP_AGENT" ]] && agent=$AICAP_AGENT`. Per-call `-a` flag already short-circuits before this, so its precedence is preserved.
- `_aiagent_autodetect` stays unchanged — `http` is opt-in and never auto-selected.
- `_ai_print_help` env-var snapshot grows four new lines (`AICAP_AGENT`, `AICAP_HTTP_URL`, `AICAP_HTTP_MODEL`, `AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY` — mask the key as `<set>`/`<unset>` so it's not echoed verbatim).
- Update the unknown-agent error string in `_aiagent_invoke` (line 162) to include `http`.
- Top-of-file comment block (lines 1-27) gets a short note on `http` and the OpenRouter / Ollama use cases.

`05_aisuggest.zsh` (line 6-9, 58-59) reuses `_aiagent_invoke` and `_aiagent_autodetect` unchanged — picks up the new agent automatically. Verify by reading the file (no edit expected).

#### 2. `scripts/aiblock.py`

- `AGENT_CONFIG` dict (lines ~63-68) gets a fifth entry `"http"` with model from `AICAP_HTTP_MODEL`. Mark it as "always available" in `detect_agents()` (lines ~79-81) when `AICAP_AGENT == "http"` or when the user explicitly picks it from the TUI — don't auto-include otherwise (no PATH probe matches).
- Spawn-agent path that builds the CLI invocation needs an `http` branch that mirrors the zsh one (use `urllib.request` from stdlib, no extra deps). Reuse zsh's metadata format on stderr for parity.
- Read `AICAP_AGENT` env var as the initial selection if set.

#### 3. Docs

- `docs/tools/aicapture.md` — add a "Provider routing" section with two concrete recipes:
  - OpenRouter free: `export AICAP_AGENT=http; export AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free; export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=…`
  - Ollama local: `export AICAP_AGENT=http; export AICAP_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions; export AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b`
- The page is already in MkDocs nav; no `mkdocs.yml` change needed (verify via `uv run mkdocs build --strict`).
- `docs/shells/aliases.md` — no rows change (no new aliases/functions, just env vars).

## Critical files

- `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh` — primary change site
- `dot_config/zsh/tools/05_aisuggest.zsh` — verify unaffected
- `scripts/aiblock.py` — parity update
- `docs/tools/aicapture.md` — env var table + recipes

## Existing utilities to reuse

- `_aicap_spinner_start` / `_aicap_spinner_stop` (lines 51-76) — wrap the curl call exactly like other branches do.
- `_aicap_prettify` (lines 80-90) — already wraps the agent reply in `_ai_dispatch_core`. No change needed; `http` reply is plain markdown text just like the other agents.
- `jq` is already a hard dep on the claude JSON path (line 107) and is in the `cli_basics` ansible role; no new install task needed.
- `curl` is universally present.

## Verification

1. **Syntax**: `zsh -n dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh` (no execution).
2. **Path-A — OpenRouter** (needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in env):
   \```
   AICAP_AGENT=http aiexplain 1
   \```
   Expect: spinner, then `http (google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free) | in=N out=N` on stderr, prettified reply on stdout.
3. **Path-B — Ollama** (needs `ollama serve` running with `qwen2.5-coder:7b` pulled):
   \```
   AICAP_AGENT=http \
   AICAP_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
   AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b \
     aiexplain 1
   \```
4. **Error path**: bad URL → curl rc≠0, stderr message, no hung spinner. Bad API key → `.error.message` surfaced verbatim.
5. **No-regression**: with `AICAP_AGENT` unset and `claude` on PATH, `aifix` still routes to claude (auto-detect path unchanged).
6. **Help text**: `aifix -h` lists the four new env vars.
7. **aiblock TUI**: launch `aiblock`, confirm `http` appears as a selectable agent when `AICAP_AGENT=http` and that the "Spawn agent" / one-shot paths both succeed against Ollama.
8. **MkDocs**: `uv run mkdocs build --strict` passes.

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#     "questionary>=2.0",
6	#     "rich>=13.9",
7	# ]
8	# ///
9	"""aiblock — pick recent shell command(s), edit a prompt, send to a coding-agent.
10	
11	UI is a short sequence of questionary prompts + rich panels:
12	  1. Pick one or more recent commands (checkbox; Space toggles, Enter confirms).
13	     Skipping the selection defaults to "last block".
14	  2. Preview the captured block(s). Multi-select concats them in chronological
15	     order (oldest first) with "--- Block -N ---" separators so the agent
16	     can tell the turns apart.
17	  3. Edit the prompt (default: "diagnose + fix").
18	  4. Choose an action: print reply / copy / spawn interactive agent / cancel.
19	
20	Advisory-only: agent is invoked with its one-shot flag so replies are text,
21	no auto-edits. To iterate further with the context pre-loaded, pick the
22	"Spawn interactive agent" action.
23	
24	Depends on:
25	  - dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh (OSC 133 markers)
26	  - dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh (cpblock)
27	  - dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh (aiblock() wrapper dumps history)
28	  - zsh on PATH (wrapper runs `fc -ln -30` in the caller's shell)
29	  - tmux (we run inside a pane)
30	  - at least one of: claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent
31	"""
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import os
35	import shutil
36	import subprocess
37	import sys
38	from dataclasses import dataclass
39	
40	import json
41	import questionary
42	from rich.console import Console
43	from rich.markdown import Markdown
44	from rich.panel import Panel
45	
46	DEFAULT_FIX_PROMPT = (
47	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. "
48	    "Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."
49	)
50	
51	# Env-var defaults mirror 04_ai_capture.zsh. If the shell has exported
52	# AICAP_*, os.environ picks them up; otherwise these defaults kick in.
53	AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL = os.environ.get("AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL", "haiku")
54	AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL = os.environ.get("AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL", "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5")
55	AICAP_CODEX_MODEL = os.environ.get("AICAP_CODEX_MODEL", "gpt-5-mini")
56	AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL = os.environ.get("AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL", "")
57	AICAP_SHOW_METADATA = os.environ.get("AICAP_SHOW_METADATA", "1") == "1"
58	AICAP_PRETTIFY = os.environ.get("AICAP_PRETTIFY", "1") == "1"
59	
60	# Each agent's non-interactive invocation args (model-aware). The Claude
61	# entry is special-cased in invoke_agent_oneshot because we optionally
62	# use --output-format json for metadata extraction.
63	AGENT_CONFIG = {
64	    "claude":       {"base": ["claude", "-p", "--model", AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL]},
65	    "opencode":     {"base": ["opencode", "run", "-m", AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL]},
66	    "codex":        {"base": ["codex", "exec", "-m", AICAP_CODEX_MODEL]},
67	    "cursor-agent": {"base": ["cursor-agent", "-p"] + (["--model", AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL] if AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL else [])},
68	}
69	
70	console = Console(stderr=False)
71	
72	
73	@dataclass
74	class HistoryEntry:
75	    n: int          # 1-based index: 1 = most recent
76	    command: str    # the command text
77	
78	
79	def detect_agents() -> list[str]:
80	    """Return the subset of known agents found on PATH, in preference order."""
81	    return [a for a in AGENT_CONFIG if shutil.which(a)]
82	
83	
84	def zsh_run(code: str, timeout: float = 5.0) -> str:
85	    """Run `zsh -ic CODE` and return stdout (strip trailing newline).
86	
87	    -ic is needed so our zsh config loads (sourcing 03_tmux_capture.zsh etc.).
88	    """
89	    # $ZDOTDIR is set by chezmoi's 00_exports; pass-through so an interactive
90	    # zsh finds the user's rc. Inherits TMUX so cpblock sees the right pane.
91	    result = subprocess.run(
92	        ["zsh", "-ic", code],
93	        capture_output=True,
94	        text=True,
95	        timeout=timeout,
96	        env=os.environ,
97	    )
98	    return result.stdout.rstrip("\n")
99	
100	
101	def list_recent_commands(n: int = 20) -> list[HistoryEntry]:
102	    """Return the last `n` shell commands as HistoryEntry(N, cmd).
103	
104	    Reads $AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP (written by the zsh `aiblock` wrapper via
105	    `fc -ln -30`) — a `zsh -ic fc …` subshell does NOT see the current
106	    shell's in-memory history, and `fc -R` from HISTFILE misses commands
107	    that haven't been flushed yet. The env-passed dump is the only
108	    reliable source for "what did the USER just run".
109	
110	    Falls back to parsing $HISTFILE directly if the dump env var isn't
111	    set (e.g. someone ran the script without the wrapper).
112	
113	    Returned list is ordered most-recent-first, with `.n` matching what
114	    cpblock/cpcmd/cpout expect as their positional N arg.
115	    """
116	    dump_path = os.environ.get("AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP")
117	    lines: list[str] = []
118	    if dump_path and os.path.isfile(dump_path):
119	        with open(dump_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
120	            lines = [ln.strip() for ln in f if ln.strip()]
121	    else:
122	        # Fallback: parse HISTFILE directly.
123	        histfile = os.environ.get("HISTFILE") or os.path.expanduser("~/.zsh_history")
124	        if os.path.isfile(histfile):
125	            with open(histfile, encoding="latin-1", errors="replace") as f:
126	                raw = f.readlines()
127	            for raw_ln in raw[-n * 3:]:  # last 3N raw lines (covers line continuations)
128	                s = raw_ln.rstrip("\n").strip()
129	                if not s:
130	                    continue
131	                # EXTENDED_HISTORY format: ": TIMESTAMP:DURATION;CMD"
132	                if s.startswith(": "):
133	                    parts = s.split(";", 1)
134	                    if len(parts) == 2:
135	                        s = parts[1]
136	                lines.append(s)
137	    # Take the last n, reverse so index 1 == most recent.
138	    lines = lines[-n:]
139	    return [HistoryEntry(n=i, command=cmd) for i, cmd in enumerate(reversed(lines), start=1)]
140	
141	
142	def capture_block(n: int) -> str:
143	    """Return cpblock N's stdout."""
144	    return zsh_run(f"cpblock {n}", timeout=10.0)
145	
146	
147	def invoke_agent_oneshot(agent: str, prompt: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
148	    """Invoke an agent in non-interactive mode; return (reply_text, metadata).
149	
150	    For Claude, we request --output-format json so we can pull usage/cost
151	    into the metadata dict. Other agents fall back to text output with a
152	    minimal metadata dict containing just the model name.
153	    """
154	    base = AGENT_CONFIG[agent]["base"]
155	    meta: dict = {"agent": agent, "model": _model_for(agent)}
156	
157	    if agent == "claude" and AICAP_SHOW_METADATA:
158	        result = subprocess.run(
159	            [*base, "--output-format", "json", prompt],
160	            capture_output=True,
161	            text=True,
162	            timeout=180.0,
163	        )
164	        if result.returncode != 0:
165	            console.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
166	            if result.stderr:
167	                console.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr}[/dim]")
168	            return "", meta
169	        try:
170	            parsed = json.loads(result.stdout)
171	            # Claude's JSON has no top-level `.model`; the actual model name
172	            # lives as the single key of `.modelUsage`.
173	            mu = parsed.get("modelUsage") or {}
174	            if mu:
175	                meta["model"] = next(iter(mu.keys()))
176	            usage = parsed.get("usage", {})
177	            meta["input_tokens"] = usage.get("input_tokens")
178	            meta["output_tokens"] = usage.get("output_tokens")
179	            meta["cache_read"] = usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens") or 0
180	            meta["cache_create"] = usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0
181	            meta["cost_usd"] = parsed.get("total_cost_usd")
182	            meta["duration_ms"] = parsed.get("duration_ms")
183	            return parsed.get("result", ""), meta
184	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
185	            return result.stdout, meta  # fall back to raw
186	
187	    result = subprocess.run(
188	        [*base, prompt],
189	        capture_output=True,
190	        text=True,
191	        timeout=180.0,
192	    )
193	    if result.returncode != 0:
194	        console.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
195	        if result.stderr:
196	            console.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr}[/dim]")
197	    return result.stdout, meta
198	
199	
200	def _model_for(agent: str) -> str:
201	    return {
202	        "claude": AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL,
203	        "opencode": AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL,
204	        "codex": AICAP_CODEX_MODEL,
205	        "cursor-agent": AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL or "(default)",
206	    }[agent]
207	
208	
209	def format_metadata(meta: dict) -> str:
210	    """Single-line metadata summary for stderr / panel subtitle."""
211	    parts = [f"{meta['agent']} ({meta['model']})"]
212	    if meta.get("input_tokens") is not None:
213	        parts.append(f"in={meta['input_tokens']}")
214	    if meta.get("output_tokens") is not None:
215	        parts.append(f"out={meta['output_tokens']}")
216	    if meta.get("cache_read") or meta.get("cache_create"):
217	        parts.append(f"cache=(r:{meta.get('cache_read', 0)},w:{meta.get('cache_create', 0)})")
218	    if meta.get("cost_usd") is not None:
219	        parts.append(f"cost=${meta['cost_usd']}")
220	    if meta.get("duration_ms") is not None:
221	        parts.append(f"{meta['duration_ms']}ms")
222	    return " | ".join(parts)
223	
224	
225	def copy_to_clipboard(text: str) -> bool:
226	    """Write text to the system clipboard. Mirror of _cpx_to_clipboard in zsh."""
227	    if os.environ.get("TMUX"):
228	        proc = subprocess.run(["tmux", "load-buffer", "-w", "-"], input=text, text=True)
229	        return proc.returncode == 0
230	    for cmd in [["pbcopy"], ["wl-copy"], ["xclip", "-selection", "clipboard", "-in"], ["xsel", "--clipboard", "--input"]]:
231	        if shutil.which(cmd[0]):
232	            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, input=text, text=True)
233	            return proc.returncode == 0
234	    return False
235	
236	
237	def spawn_interactive_agent(agent: str, context: str, prompt: str) -> None:
238	    """Open a new tmux window running `agent` with block + prompt pre-loaded.
239	
240	    Implementation: write context+prompt to a temp file, start the agent in a
241	    new tmux window with a shell that cats the file to the agent's stdin,
242	    then execs the interactive agent. This gives the user an ongoing session
243	    seeded with the context.
244	    """
245	    if not os.environ.get("TMUX"):
246	        console.print("[red]Spawn requires tmux.[/red]")
247	        return
248	    import tempfile
249	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", delete=False, suffix=".txt") as f:
250	        f.write(prompt + "\n\n" + context + "\n")
251	        ctx_file = f.name
252	    # Build an appropriate interactive invocation per agent. This is
253	    # best-effort — agents vary in how they accept piped context. The
254	    # common pattern: paste context into the first user message, then
255	    # continue interactively.
256	    # For now, launch the agent plain in a new window and drop the context
257	    # file path into the window title so the user can paste it with Enter.
258	    title = f"ai:{agent}"
259	    # Try to pre-paste context via tmux paste-buffer: load the file into a
260	    # named buffer, start the agent, then paste the buffer.
261	    subprocess.run(["tmux", "load-buffer", "-b", "aiblock", ctx_file])
262	    subprocess.run([
263	        "tmux", "new-window", "-n", title,
264	        f"{agent}; rm -f {ctx_file}",
265	    ])
266	    console.print(
267	        f"[green]Opened new tmux window '{title}' running {agent}.[/green]\n"
268	        f"[dim]Context in tmux paste-buffer 'aiblock' — "
269	        f"press `prefix + =` to choose it, or `tmux paste-buffer -b aiblock`.[/dim]"
270	    )
271	
272	
273	def main() -> int:
274	    if "--help" in sys.argv or "-h" in sys.argv:
275	        console.print(__doc__)
276	        return 0
277	
278	    if not os.environ.get("TMUX"):
279	        console.print("[red]aiblock must run inside a tmux pane (uses cpblock).[/red]")
280	        return 1
281	
282	    agents = detect_agents()
283	    if not agents:
284	        console.print(
285	            "[red]No coding-agent CLI on PATH.[/red]\n"
286	            "[dim]Install one of: claude, opencode, codex, cursor-agent.[/dim]"
287	        )
288	        return 1
289	
290	    history = list_recent_commands(n=20)
291	    if not history:
292	        console.print("[red]Shell history is empty — no commands to pick from.[/red]")
293	        return 1
294	
295	    # 1. Pick one or more commands (multi-select via checkbox).
296	    # Space toggles, Enter accepts; picking zero falls back to "last block".
297	    choices = [
298	        questionary.Choice(
299	            title=f"{h.n:>2}  {h.command[:100]}",
300	            value=h.n,
301	        )
302	        for h in history
303	    ]
304	    picked = questionary.checkbox(
305	        "Pick command(s) to review (Space toggles, Enter confirms):",
306	        choices=choices,
307	        qmark="▸",
308	    ).ask()
309	    if picked is None:
310	        return 1
311	    if not picked:
312	        picked = [1]  # default to most recent
313	
314	    # Sort descending so the OLDEST-first chronological order when we iterate
315	    # (N=5 is older than N=1; we want history-order concat).
316	    picked_ns = sorted(set(picked), reverse=True)
317	
318	    # 2. Capture each block + show a combined preview. Concat with separators
319	    # so the agent can see boundaries.
320	    blocks: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
321	    for n in picked_ns:
322	        text = capture_block(n)
323	        if not text.strip():
324	            console.print(
325	                f"[yellow]cpblock {n} returned empty — skipping.[/yellow]"
326	            )
327	            continue
328	        blocks.append((n, text.rstrip()))
329	    if not blocks:
330	        console.print(
331	            "[red]All selected blocks were empty.[/red]\n"
332	            "[dim]Try `exec zsh` if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, "
333	            "or pick different indices.[/dim]"
334	        )
335	        return 1
336	
337	    # Single-block: preserve the original Panel shape. Multi-block: show each
338	    # in its own Panel so boundaries are obvious before the user commits.
339	    if len(blocks) == 1:
340	        n, text = blocks[0]
341	        console.print(Panel(text, title=f"Block -{n}", expand=False))
342	        block = text
343	    else:
344	        for n, text in blocks:
345	            console.print(Panel(text, title=f"Block -{n}", expand=False))
346	        # Agent sees: --- Block -5 ---\n<text>\n\n--- Block -3 ---\n<text>
347	        # Picking a clear separator helps the model know these are distinct
348	        # turns rather than one long transcript.
349	        block = "\n\n".join(
350	            f"--- Block -{n} ---\n{text}" for n, text in blocks
351	        )
352	
353	    # 3. Edit the prompt
354	    prompt = questionary.text(
355	        "Prompt (edit or accept):",
356	        default=DEFAULT_FIX_PROMPT,
357	        multiline=True,
358	    ).ask()
359	    if prompt is None:
360	        return 1
361	
362	    # 4. Choose agent if multiple available
363	    if len(agents) > 1:
364	        agent = questionary.select(
365	            "Agent:",
366	            choices=agents,
367	            default=agents[0],
368	        ).ask()
369	        if agent is None:
370	            return 1
371	    else:
372	        agent = agents[0]
373	
374	    # 5. Choose action
375	    action = questionary.select(
376	        "Action:",
377	        choices=[
378	            questionary.Choice("Print reply here", value="print"),
379	            questionary.Choice("Copy reply to clipboard", value="copy"),
380	            questionary.Choice(f"Spawn new tmux window running {agent} with context", value="spawn"),
381	            questionary.Choice("Cancel", value="cancel"),
382	        ],
383	    ).ask()
384	    if action in (None, "cancel"):
385	        return 0
386	
387	    full_prompt = f"{prompt}\n\n{block}"
388	
389	    if action == "spawn":
390	        spawn_interactive_agent(agent, block, prompt)
391	        return 0
392	
393	    # Print / Copy both need the agent to actually reply
394	    with console.status(f"[cyan]Asking {_model_for(agent)}…[/cyan]", spinner="dots"):
395	        reply, meta = invoke_agent_oneshot(agent, full_prompt)
396	
397	    if not reply.strip():
398	        console.print("[yellow]Agent returned empty reply.[/yellow]")
399	        return 1
400	
401	    subtitle = format_metadata(meta) if AICAP_SHOW_METADATA else None
402	
403	    if action == "print":
404	        # Render markdown so headings / code fences / lists look right.
405	        if AICAP_PRETTIFY:
406	            console.print(
407	                Panel(
408	                    Markdown(reply.rstrip()),
409	                    title=f"{agent} reply",
410	                    subtitle=subtitle,
411	                    expand=False,
412	                )
413	            )
414	        else:
415	            console.print(
416	                Panel(reply.rstrip(), title=f"{agent} reply", subtitle=subtitle, expand=False)
417	            )
418	    elif action == "copy":
419	        ok = copy_to_clipboard(reply)
420	        if ok:
421	            msg = f"[green]Copied {len(reply)} bytes to clipboard.[/green]"
422	            if subtitle:
423	                msg += f"\n[dim]{subtitle}[/dim]"
424	            console.print(msg)
425	        else:
426	            console.print("[red]No clipboard tool available.[/red]")
427	            return 1
428	    return 0
429	
430	
431	if __name__ == "__main__":
432	    try:
433	        sys.exit(main())
434	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
435	        sys.exit(130)
436

```text
1	# aicapture — AI review of past shell commands
2	
3	Capture a past shell command's block from tmux scrollback, pipe it to a coding-agent CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor Agent) in non-interactive mode, get back a fix or explanation. Advisory by default: agent prints suggestions, doesn't touch files.
4	
5	Built on [OSC 133 semantic prompts](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md) — the shell emits `A`/`C`/`D` line-attribute markers, tmux stores them, our helpers navigate by them. For background on how this compares to `thefuck`, Warp, `wut`, `tmuxai`, `atuin`, etc., see [instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md](../this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md).
6	
7	> **Why not Charm [`mods`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/mods)?** `mods` is a generic CLI LLM client. We deliberately route through the existing agent CLIs (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor Agent) instead, because they own the per-tool model selection, system prompts, tool permissions, and project context that `aifix` / `aiexplain` rely on. `aicapture` is a tmux-scrollback capture layer, not a model-routing layer; the agent CLIs already handle the routing. Auto-detection chain lives in `dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`.
8	
9	## Quick start
10	
11	```sh
12	# Any command that produced useful output or an error…
13	cargo build --release
14	
15	# …is one keystroke away from a diagnose + fix:
16	aifix
17	```
18	
19	Output in your terminal:
20	
21	```
22	aifix ← block -1
23	⠋ claude haiku (json)…                                  # spinner while agent thinks
24	claude (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) | in=12 out=87 cache=(r:24402,w:12487) | cost=$0.0008 3812ms
25	
26	## Fix for `cargo build` error
27	
28	Your `Cargo.toml` is missing the `serde` dependency. Add:
29	
30	    [dependencies]
31	    serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
32	
33	Then re-run `cargo build --release`.
34	```
35	
36	Reply is rendered as Markdown via `glow` (auto-falls back to `bat --language=md`, then raw text if neither is installed).
37	
38	## Commands
39	
40	### Capture (no AI call)
41	
42	Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly) **and** copies it to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge (works over SSH). Defaults to N=1 (most recent); pass a positive integer for N-back lookback.
43	
44	| Command | Scope |
45	|---|---|
46	| `cpcmd [N]` | Nth-latest command's **input line** (from zsh history — works outside tmux too) |
47	| `cpout [N]` | Nth-latest command's **output** only (via tmux + OSC 133) |
48	| `cpblock [N]` | Nth-latest command's **full block**: prompt + input + output (Warp-style) |
49	
50	```sh
51	cpblock                          # last block → clipboard + stdout
52	cpblock 3                        # 3rd-latest
53	cpout 2 | tee /tmp/snapshot.log  # pipe output to file while also copying
54	cpcmd                            # just the command string (no output)
55	```
56	
57	### AI review
58	
59	Same positional `[N]` as the capture helpers, plus flags:
60	
61	| Command | Default prompt |
62	|---|---|
63	| `aifix [N]` | *"Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."* |
64	| `aiexplain [N]` | *"Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise."* |
65	
66	Both accept:
67	
68	- `-a AGENT` — `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` / `cursor-agent`. Default: auto-detect (first one found on `$PATH`).
69	- `-p PROMPT` — override the default prompt.
70	- `--raw` — skip glow/bat prettify; print the agent's raw Markdown text.
71	- `--no-meta` — suppress the stderr metadata line (model / tokens / cost / duration).
72	- `-h` / `--help` — print the full signature and current env-var values.
73	
74	```sh
75	aifix                               # last block, default fix prompt
76	aifix 3 -a opencode                 # 3rd-latest, force OpenCode
77	aifix -p "is this safe on prod?"    # custom prompt
78	aiexplain 2 --raw                   # no prettify
79	aifix --no-meta | tee /tmp/ans.md   # pipe-friendly
80	```
81	
82	### Interactive TUI
83	
84	```sh
85	aiblock
86	```
87	
88	Launches a [questionary](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary) + [rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich) TUI ([`scripts/aiblock.py`](../../scripts/aiblock.py)) that walks through:
89	
90	1. **Checkbox picker** over the last 20 commands. Space toggles, Enter confirms. Picking none defaults to "last block".
91	2. **Preview** — each selected block shown in its own rich panel (multi-select concatenates in chronological order with `--- Block -N ---` separators so the agent can tell the turns apart).
92	3. **Prompt edit** — default is the `aifix` fix-prompt; edit inline.
93	4. **Action** — one of:
94	   - *Print reply here* — rendered as Markdown in a rich panel with the metadata as subtitle.
95	   - *Copy reply to clipboard* — via tmux OSC 52 / pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy.
96	   - *Spawn new tmux window running `<agent>`* — opens a fresh interactive agent session with your selected blocks pre-loaded into tmux's `aiblock` paste-buffer. Pull via `prefix + =`.
97	
98	The TUI depends on `uv` (PEP 723 inline deps) — no separate install step required; first run populates the uv cache.
99	
100	## Non-tmux alternatives
101	
102	When you're not in tmux (VSCode integrated terminal, bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH session), `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` can't see scrollback — they depend on tmux's OSC 133 line attributes. Three Tier 1 wrappers cover the common cases without magic (no shell hooks, no PTY proxy, no `script(1)` wrapping — see [`backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md`](../../backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md) for why we reject those paths):
103	
104	| Command | Source of context | Typical use |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| `aifix-stdin` | whatever you pipe in | `tail -100 build.log \| aifix-stdin` |
107	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | runs `CMD`, tees stdout+stderr to a log, reviews | `aifix-run -- cargo build --release` |
108	| `aifix-rerun` | re-executes the previous shell command (confirm prompt) | `aifix-rerun` after a transient error |
109	
110	All three accept the same flags as `aifix` (`-a AGENT` / `-p PROMPT` / `--raw` / `--no-meta`). `aifix-rerun` adds `-y` to skip the "⚠ side effects" confirmation. Default prompt for each is the `aifix` "diagnose + fix"; use `-p "explain what happened"` if you want the explain behaviour.
111	
112	```sh
113	# stdin — compose with any producer
114	tail -200 /var/log/nginx/error.log | aifix-stdin
115	curl -sS https://weird.api/thing | aifix-stdin -p "what is this JSON telling me?"
116	aifix-stdin < /tmp/build-fail.log
117	
118	# run — capture a fresh invocation (double-run safe, no prior history needed)
119	aifix-run -- ls /missing
120	aifix-run -p "is this safe on prod?" -- ansible-playbook deploy.yml
121	
122	# rerun — thefuck-style, re-execute last cmd. Confirms by default.
123	mvn compile      # fails
124	aifix-rerun      # "⚠ side effects…  Proceed? [y/N]"
125	aifix-rerun -y   # skip confirm
126	```
127	
128	**isatty caveat** for `aifix-run`: teeing makes CMD's stdout a pipe, so TUI apps (vim, less, htop) render in degraded mode. Don't `aifix-run` an interactive tool — pipe its log file via `aifix-stdin` after the fact instead.
129	
130	**Side-effect warning** for `aifix-rerun`: re-running `rm`, `curl -X POST`, `git push`, migrations, etc. is dangerous. The confirmation prompt is there for a reason; don't `-y` without reading what will be re-executed.
131	
132	## Configuration
133	
134	Put any of these in `~/.zshrc`, a `99_local_*.zsh` override, or export them per-session:
135	
136	```sh
137	# Model per agent (auto-detected order: claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent)
138	export AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=haiku                              # alias or full name (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6)
139	export AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL=github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5  # provider/model format
140	export AICAP_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5-mini
141	export AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL=                                    # empty = cursor-agent picks
142	
143	# Output behaviour
144	export AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1   # 0 to mute the stderr "claude (...) | in=... cost=..." line
145	export AICAP_PRETTIFY=1        # 0 to always print raw Markdown (skip glow/bat)
146	export AICAP_SPINNER=1         # 0 to disable the stderr spinner animation
147	```
148	
149	Check current settings any time with `aifix --help`.
150	
151	Defaults are tuned for Haiku-class models — fast (~5s round-trip) and cheap (~$0.001/call with cache hits). If you want Opus/Sonnet for harder diagnoses, set `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet` either globally or per-invocation:
152	
153	```sh
154	AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet aifix 3
155	```
156	
157	## Requirements
158	
159	| What | For |
160	|---|---|
161	| `zsh` | All commands (cpcmd, aifix, etc. are zsh functions) |
162	| `tmux 3.3+` | `cpout` / `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` (scrollback navigation) |
163	| OSC 133 shell integration | The hook in `dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh` emits the A/C/D markers tmux needs. Run `exec zsh` after install so the hook fires in your current shell. |
164	| At least one coding-agent CLI | `claude` (recommended), `opencode`, `codex`, or `cursor-agent` — install via your usual channel |
165	| `glow` (optional) | Markdown prettify on agent replies |
166	| `bat` (optional) | Prettify fallback when `glow` isn't present |
167	| `jq` (optional) | Parses Claude's `--output-format json` for the metadata line (tokens / cost) |
168	| `uv` (optional) | Needed only for the `aiblock` TUI — installs its Python deps lazily |
169	
170	## Standalone setup (no chezmoi)
171	
172	If you don't want to adopt the whole dotfiles repo, grab these four files and source them from your `~/.zshrc`. They're self-contained apart from the listed optional tools above.
173	
174	```sh
175	REPO=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main
176	mkdir -p ~/.config/zsh/tools
177	
178	# Shell side: OSC 133 hook + cpblock family + aifix family
179	for f in 02_shell_integration.zsh 03_tmux_capture.zsh 04_ai_capture.zsh; do
180	  curl -fsSL "$REPO/dot_config/zsh/tools/$f" -o "$HOME/.config/zsh/tools/$f"
181	done
182	
183	# Optional TUI (needs uv)
184	mkdir -p ~/.local/share/aicapture
185	curl -fsSL "$REPO/scripts/aiblock.py" -o ~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py
186	chmod +x ~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py
187	
188	# Append to ~/.zshrc (or equivalent)
189	cat >> ~/.zshrc <<'EOF'
190	for f in ~/.config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh \
191	         ~/.config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh \
192	         ~/.config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh; do
193	  [[ -r "$f" ]] && source "$f"
194	done
195	EOF
196	
197	# Reload
198	exec zsh
199	```
200	
201	The `aiblock` shell function resolves the TUI path via `chezmoi source-path`; if you're not on chezmoi, edit the `aiblock()` function in `04_ai_capture.zsh` to point at `~/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py` instead:
202	
203	```zsh
204	# replace the chezmoi source-path block with:
205	_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT="$HOME/.local/share/aicapture/aiblock.py"
206	```
207	
208	### Read source on GitHub
209	
210	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh) — OSC 133 precmd/preexec hooks (A marker embedded in `$PROMPT` via `%{...%}` — see [`pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/zsh-osc133-precmd-printf-a-not-stored.md) for why)
211	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh) — cpout / cpcmd / cpblock + tmux copy-mode chain helpers
212	- [`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh) — aifix / aiexplain / aiblock wrappers, agent dispatch, spinner
213	- [`scripts/aiblock.py`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/scripts/aiblock.py) — Python TUI (PEP 723 inline deps)
214	
215	## Troubleshooting
216	
217	### `cpblock returned empty` / `aifix ← block -1` then nothing
218	
219	Your current shell was started before the hook was installed. The precmd/preexec hooks that emit OSC 133 markers need to be registered via `add-zsh-hook`, which only happens when `02_shell_integration.zsh` is sourced. Fix:
220	
221	```sh
222	exec zsh                                             # reload shell in place
223	echo $precmd_functions | tr ' ' '\n' | grep osc133   # verify
224	# expected: _osc133_precmd
225	```
226	
227	If `exec zsh` doesn't help, open a fresh tmux window — some terminal states don't propagate cleanly through `exec`.
228	
229	### `aiblock`: "Shell history is empty — no commands to pick from"
230	
231	Should no longer happen after commit `3993b7b`. If it does, the zsh wrapper that dumps history via `fc -ln -30` isn't running. Verify:
232	
233	```sh
234	which aiblock     # should show the function from 04_ai_capture.zsh
235	type aiblock      # should show the fc-dump logic
236	```
237	
238	Workaround: the TUI also falls back to parsing `$HISTFILE` directly, so `HISTFILE=~/.zsh_history aiblock` works even if the wrapper is broken.
239	
240	### Metadata line shows `claude (?)` instead of the model
241	
242	`jq` failed to find `.modelUsage | keys | first` in Claude's JSON output. Either `jq` is out of date (install latest) or Claude CLI changed its JSON shape. Set `AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=0` to bypass until fixed.
243	
244	### Spinner doesn't appear / doesn't disappear
245	
246	Spinner auto-skips when stderr isn't a tty. If you're redirecting with `2>/tmp/err` or piping through `tee` you won't see it — by design.
247	
248	If the spinner leaves a stale `⠋ ...` line after the agent returns, the `kill $_AICAP_SPIN_PID` + `\r\e[K` cleanup didn't run (usually because of a signal during a subshell). Press `Ctrl+L` to redraw, then report it.
249	
250	### tmux scrollback looks "broken" / ghost frames
251	
252	Not directly an aicapture issue but adjacent — see [`pitfalls/tmux-scrollback-tui-repaint-ghosting.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/tmux-scrollback-tui-repaint-ghosting.md) and the `scroll-on-clear off` + `prefix + [` workflow.
253

Implementation complete. Summary:

**`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`**
- New `http` agent in `_aiagent_invoke` that POSTs to an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint via `curl` + `jq` (covers OpenRouter + Ollama with the same code path).
- `AICAP_AGENT` env var honored by all three dispatchers (`_ai_capture_dispatch`, `aifix-stdin`, `aifix-run`); auto-detect order unchanged. Per-call `-a` still wins.
- New env vars `AICAP_HTTP_URL` / `AICAP_HTTP_MODEL` / `AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY` (falls back to `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`). All listed in `aifix --help`.

**`scripts/aiblock.py`**
- Mirrors the zsh changes via `urllib` (no new deps). `http` only appears in the agent picker when `AICAP_AGENT=http` is set. "Spawn interactive" refuses for `http` since there's no CLI to launch.

**`docs/tools/aicapture.md`**
- New "Provider routing: OpenRouter / Ollama" section with concrete recipes for both. Updated `-a AGENT` list, env-var snippet, and Requirements table.

**Verified**
- `zsh -n` syntax pass
- `python3 -c ast.parse` syntax pass  
- `aifix --help` renders all new env vars correctly
- Error path: bad URL → `curl rc=7`, clear stderr message, no hung spinner
- AICAP_AGENT=http takes effect through `aifix-stdin` (and by extension all dispatchers)
- `mkdocs build --strict` warnings are all pre-existing (verified by stash + rebuild)

Quickstart for you:

```sh
# OpenRouter free Gemini Flash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...
AICAP_AGENT=http aifix

# Local Ollama
AICAP_AGENT=http \
  AICAP_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b aifix
```
